#1925. Bradford City 4 York City 0: Clean EFL Trophy sweep for Bantams who show ruthless side again

BD8 was packed to the rafters just 10 days earlier for Bradford City’s juicy league meeting with Huddersfield Town.

On this occasion, in front of an understandably sparse crowd, the atmosphere was low octane in comparison.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

For those that ventured out, including a decent-sized following of almost 700 supporters from the walled city - with York making their first visit to this part of West Yorkshire since October 2012 - it proved worth their while, even if there was little riding on this final Northern Group C game.

Bradford were through, most likely as group winners unless something silly happened. Which it definitely didn’t.

A first-half opener from returning captain Antoni Sarcevic - whose three goals this term have all been on home soil - put the hosts on their way to a clean sweep of group victories.

A third cup strike of the campaign for Stephen Humphrys rubber-stamped the win before another striker with a penchant for goals in knock-out football this season in Will Swan provided gloss.

Swan’s 70th-minute strike, nine minutes after Humphrys’ goal, took his season’s goal tally to seven, with just one in the league.

Substitute Nick Powell joined in the goalscoring action before the end after his midweek brace in the cup against Marine. He is now one shy of double figures.

It was a rewarding night for Michael Duff’s side, whose next two fixtures arrive against White Rose visitors in the shape of Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley. This was a decent warm-up.

With the pressure maybe off a touch, both sets of players among much-changed line-ups, showed good things for the first hour, more especially those in claret and amber.

York’s wait for a first away win on their league return goes on, as does their run without a victory in Bradford - the Minstermen last won here in March 1980.

For 60 minutes, they gave a good account of themselves before the Bantams showed the ruthless edge which mauled Marine. The scoreline was cruel on them on the night.

City made ten changes from their handsome cup slaying of Marine, with Kieran Morgan being the only player who lined up against the Merseysiders.

It was a notable night for Iraq under-23 goalkeeper Zac Hadi, handed a Bantams debut, while Harry Ibbitson started for the first time at Valley Parade.

Fresh from his one-match suspension, Sarcevic got a run-out for the hosts, inactive after this fixture until November 21.

Unlike the Bantams, York were mindful of forthcoming weekend league business at Rochdale. Scott Lindsey not only changed his entire XI from the weekend cup victory over Northampton Town, but gave them the complete night off with none on the bench either.

The Minstermen gave a debut to youngster Lewis Beadle, with keeper George Sykes-Kenworthy getting the nod in goal at the club where he started out.

Bradford led at the break, but both sides contributed to a very watchable contest, more especially given that it was a ‘dead rubber’.

The Bantams and their visitors both hit the woodwork. York played some neat passing football at times, but it was the hosts who drew first blood with an elegant 32nd-minute opener.

The hosts broke with intent and Swan’s perceptive left-wing cross found Humphreys, who spotted Sarcevic in space and found him with a lovely weighted pass and the home captain finished clinically, low past Sykes-Kenworthy - as befitting a goalscoring midfielder of his ilk. It was a quality move and finish.

Humphreys and Sarcevic had some fun in the final period of the half and had further chances, with York starting to look a bit wary. They had brought offerings to the table before that at the other end.

Hadi was forced into significant work to make a strong double save to deny Jovan Malcolm and Joe Grey before producing a textbook parry - and positioning - to keep out Dipo Akinyemi’s goalbound header.

Earlier, York knocked on wood from close range, courtesy of Ethan Shiver. As did Bradford earlier, with Kieran Morgan displaying sublime technique to warm up a nippy November night. His exquisite shot with the outside of his foot clipped the post.

Half-time came at a more convenient juncture for York than the hosts. But it was Bradford who carried on from where they left off ahead of the interval, with Morgan - having a handy game - finding Swan, whose rasping shot stung the palms of Sykes-Kenworthy.

The York custodian was then called into action again to beat out Humphrys’ angled drive, with Sarcevic’s follow-up header hitting the underside of the bar.

In keeping with an entertaining evening, York should have levelled moments later.

Malcolm broke away and went for glory instead of slotting in Akinyemi. Hadi, in keeping with his good night, made himself big and made the point-blank save.

It’s importance was soon magnified when Humphreys’ header doubled the hosts lead just after the hour mark following Reece Welsh’s right-wing centre.

It was Humphrys' last involvement of the night.

Swan tucked home a third following substitute Powell’s cross after the Minstermen were opened up.

City gave debuts off the bench in the final quarter to two youngsters in Leeroy Gomes, Gabe Holt and Oliver Hewitt.

Powell added an effortless late fourth after clever play by the impressive Morgan. A rewarding night for Bradford.

Bradford City: Hadi; Welch, Matthews, Pratt (Hewitt 85); Ibbitson, Cartwright, Morgan, O'Keeffe (Holt 77); Sarcevic (Lunn 62), Swan (Gomes 77); Humphrys (Powell 62). Substitutes unused: Doyle, Gillesphey.

York City: Sykes-Kenworthy; J Hunt, Beadle, Medley (Belleh 62); King, Maguire, Stiver, Grey (Farrar 62), Newby; Malcolm, Akinyemi. Substitutes unused: White, Swansbury, Ozisik, Penrose, Appleyard.

#1924. Photo: Leak suggests Puma will go for bold design with Milan’s 2027-28 third kit

The design of AC Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season has been leaked, according to a report, featuring a black base and yellow details.

The 2027-28 season will be the last with Puma as Milan’s kit partner, as an agreement worth €50m per year has been reached with Adidas from 2028-29 onwards. It’s a switch that many fans have longed for, but right now, the focus is on whether Puma will end their tenure at the top or not.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The reality is that a lot of the Puma kits, especially the ones in recent years, have been praised by the Milan fans for their design. There’s certainly no bad blood between the parties and as such, Puma is working very hard to deliver a strong output for the last season.

This morning, an image of what is believed to be Milan’s third kit for the 2027-28 season surfaced, courtesy of the usually credible Footy Headlines. The base is black with grey paint splatter effects, while the details are yellow/neon-yellow.

It doesn’t really remind us of any previous kits that Milan have worn, especially since it’s a rather bold design (but it’s a third kit, after all). Compared to the current third kit, for example, the 2026-27 edition is much more muted and clean, whereas this is very lively.

Only the chest image has been leaked so far, so we will have to wait a little longer to see the full shirt. Let’s also remember that this is an early leak and that the final design will likely differ a little. Usually, the final version tends to look better.

#1922. 'Real blow': Bradford City boss Michael Duff's unwelcome injury update to tarnish EFL Trophy win over York City

Pointon came off in the first half and scans have revealed an MCL injury, Duff confirmed after his side's 4-0 win over York City in the club's final EFL Trophy Northern Group C fixture on Tuesday evening.

The City chief also revealed that Cam Dawson will be out for four weeks after pulling his calf ahead of the warm-up on Saturday. That resulted in Zac Hadi being handed his competitive debut in goal against the Minstermen, with Jon McCracken on international business.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Meanwhile, George Lapslie could be sidelined for four weeks with a hamstring injury.

Duff has at least been afforded some good news with Josh Neufville (hamstring), out since September 19, set to return for the Yorkshire derby at home to Doncaster Rovers on November 21.

Duff said: "Bobby is the real blow. Bobby's going to be (out) eight weeks, minimum.

"But we're waiting to see a result. He's off to see a specialist, so we need to see what the results of that are. The scans show it's an MCL, so it's not great news.

"Josh Neufville will be available now. He's been full training.

"He's been with the sports scientist all up until about a week ago, where he's getting sort of match distances and match numbers, unopposed. Then he's trained fully for the last three or four days. And then doing extras on top of that as well.

"So he'll be a big plus. But obviously, you don't want to lose two for every one that you get back. But it's football.

"Everyone gets injuries, it's how you react to them. Cam's (injury) is four weeks.

"Laps, we think, is going to be about four weeks (out) with his hamstring."

City confirmed top spot - and a home draw - in the knock-out phases following a convincing win over York, with Antoni Sarcevic, Stephen Humphrys, Will Swan and Nick Powell all netting for the hosts, who scored three goals in the last half-hour.

It took the Bantams' haul of goals in their past two cup/trophy games to 11.

Alongside Hadi, academy products Leeroy Gomes, Gabe Holt and Oliver Hewitt made their debuts, while Harry Ibbitson was handed his home bow.

Duff said: "After the first 15 minutes, we were really good.

"We didn't quite get the press right on a couple of bits in the first 15 minutes but after that, it was really positive night. Clean sheet, I think that's eight clean sheets in nine games. Four goals, four senior attacking players scoring four goals.

"Five debuts, seven academy players on the pitch... Top of the group, and a crowd of two-and-a-half thousand here as well, which you didn't expect. So I thought it was a good game.

#1921. Thomas Tuchel admits his relationship with Jude Bellingham is 'up and down' - but on the mend - as he reveals he's apologised to Kobbie Mainoo who is struggling at 'off a cliff' Man United

Published: 14:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 15:27 EST, 6 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel says his rocky relationship with Jude Bellingham is on the mend after revealing he called his brother Jobe in to the England squad after some cajoling from the Real Madrid star.

Tuchel and Bellingham Snr have not always seen eye to eye during the German's time as England boss.

But Tuchel said today he hopes those days are behind him after he called 21-year-old Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe into this squad for next week's Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

'It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place,' said Tuchel.

'I love to be his coach. He's a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways. If Jude was not feeling comfortable he would not perform on that level.

'In the moment you see he's happy to come into camp, he's happy with the role he has, he's fully invested and now to have the chance to have both of them is just the next step.

Thomas Tuchel has admitted he has an up and down relationship with Jude Bellingham

'I hope we have finished with the down. You never know as a coach!'

With injury to Bournemouth's Alex Scott and Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for Thursday's Croatia game at Wembley, Tuchel sprung a surprise by elevating Jobe Bellingham from the Under 21s to the senior squad.

'Yeah Jude and I have spoken about his brother because I was aware it was always his dream to play with Jobe for England,' explained Tuchel.

'Jude was always saying: "Watch him, watch him he's good, he can make it". 'I would say: "Yeah we are watching him".

'I think he actually watched training very early in my reign. He came over and watched his brother train. We chatted and said it would be nice if one day he was with him.

'He was very kind and very polite and I'm glad to have him in camp. Everyone will compare them and he has to live with this.

Now Tuchel says he 'loves' to be Bellingham's coach after his brilliant World Cup campaign

Jude had a hand in brother Jobe being called up to the England squad for the first time

'They look similar, even in their movements, but they are very different players. Jobe is more defensive. I think they are also different characters, at least that's what I heard.

'He couldn't stop smiling when I called to tell him the news. He has the same beautiful smile like Jude so it's nice to have him.'

Tuchel's squad for what he insists are two important games was once again full of messages and insights into this thinking.

There was no room for Cole Palmer and Kobbie Mainoo after both players withdrew from the October campo with injuries. There was also no call up once again for Manchester City's Phil Foden.

Asked about Palmer, fit and ready now and in decent form at Chelsea, Tuchel said: 'It's not personal and we will never assume that he is not desperate to come and play.

'But the competition is on. It's about the ones who walk the walk and come to camp.

'Someone more intelligent once said to me: 'You cannot not communicate. You cannot not send a message.'

'So yeah. A nomination is always a message, yes.'

Tuchel revealed that he almost picked Foden – who hasn't played for England since March – after an upturn in his form but had second thoughts when he saw him relegated back to the bench at the Etihad Stadium.

'He is close and he will always be close,' said Tuchel.

'There were glimpses of the Phil Foden that we would love to see. He had these two matches with four or five goal involvements and assists and being so clinical.

Cole Palmer continues to be left out by Tuchel - while Phil Foden was close to a recall

'I got excited and thought: "That's it, that's, he found his mojo, he is getting back there". Then he dropped again and played again from the bench.

'I'm in love with him as a player. What is not to love?

'If you see the boy train it's just the highest, highest quality.

'But we're talking about numbers in an England shirt which are not in proportion to his talent and to his potential.

'If we can align this and become a regular City starter and be decisive, I think he has to be always an option.

'It was very close and it's also close for Eberechi Eze to keep his place with us. He's not starting for Arsenal.

'But the advantage was maybe that Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze come again into camp. The advantage was that they have been in camp last time.'

Thomas Tuchel has told how he apologised in front of the whole England squad to Kobbie Mainoo for not giving him a single minute during the summer's World Cup in America.

Mainoo cut a lost and frustrated figure during England's campaign after a succession of players were picked ahead of him in his central midfield position.

The Manchester United star has not made Tuchel's squad for the forthcoming Nations League games with Croatia and Spain after withdrawing from the last camp with injury.

Tuchel revealed: 'He was hugely disappointed from the World Cup, and deservedly so.

'I said it in front of the team, in front of the staff.

'I said: "Sorry that I didn't pick you, you did nothing wrong, that is on me".

'He was disappointed and I think it cost him a bit of confidence.

Tuchel has noted how Man United 'fell off a cliff' - causing issues for Kobbie Mainoo

'He was excellent in training and in the way he presented himself through the tournament.

'So he was never a problem, the way he carried himself.

'Then he pulled out of last camp. I was desperate to give him the minutes. Desperate to include him in this new start, in the Nations League.

'But he then missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

'He was injured then Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he suffers from that.'

#1920. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

There has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

That is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

There was a fist pump from Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge and we are moments away from kick-off in west London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Luka Modric has hinted that he could continue playing beyond this season, having made Milan his home since arriving in 2025.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A few months ago, Modric also announced that he would continue with the Croatian national team, deciding not to retire after the World Cup. It’s a pretty clear signal that he still feels in great shape and perhaps could continue beyond this season.

“It was a fantastic victory and I think it was our best performance of the season. We deserved these three points, which we really needed, both for our morale and for our confidence.

“We are putting the coach’s ideas into practice better and better, we are moving in the right direction, and our stadium is driving us: the Milan fans are incredible.”

“I feel good and I still have the passion, ambition, and strength. As long as I feel this way, I want to keep playing. I’m also loved at Milan. I had no doubts this summer, after speaking with Amorim and the club: they wanted me to stay and I just needed to feel wanted.

“Milan is my team, and I want to help the younger players develop,” he stated.

#1917. 'I can't lie' - Leeds United winger Daniel James lifts lid on frustration of not playing

Leeds United winger Daniel James has conceded there is frustration that comes with a lack of playing time.

The jet-heeled wideman is rated highly by Whites boss Daniel Farke and has been a key figure throughout the German’s reign.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, he has found opportunities limited this season and managed just one start in the Premier League.

James, now away on international duty with Wales, has discussed the importance of being a team player in an interview with the official Leeds website.

The 29-year-old said: “I think we've had a great start. I think it was very important for us to get a result coming to this international break. I thought we were really good, put on a great performance.

“But yeah, as a player, obviously, I can't lie, obviously you do get frustrated not playing, but you have to give your all for the team, because ultimately it's a team game and, even if you're not getting as many minutes as you want, you want to perform and train every day, push players that are starting as well.

“I played against Bournemouth, a couple of weeks ago. I felt really good, but ultimately it's always down to the manager of what team he wants to set up in. But I've just got to be ready every time, and I feel like I am.

“I've got myself in a good place to whenever I'm called upon, that I feel ready. And I feel really good coming to this camp.”

James will turn 30 next year and has the additional responisibilites that come with being a senior player. Not only does he have plenty of experience, the former Swansea City star is Leeds’ longest-serving player having joined from Manchester United back in 2021.

He said: “I'm definitely just as quick. I think obviously I've had a few injuries and sometimes it's taken me a little bit longer [to recover], but I think, as I become more of a senior player, it's about how much you can maintain that, because I think it's not just about being quick once. You want to be able to do that the whole game.

"And I think as I've become more senior, I've learned to work around that a lot more. But it's something that I work on every day because, ultimately, I want to play, I want my career to be as long as possible. But I want to be as quick as long as possible.

“I think when you start getting 30 plus, I think it's about how much you can maintain it. But it's something that I'm always working on, and will do for the rest of my career.”

#1916. Midweek magic follows weekend woe as Eastbourne Borough down Dulwich Hamlet

For Borough supporters, loyalty comes with a sou'wester and a set of waterproofs: only a week ago, after the gale-blown victory over Stanway Rovers, manager Steve King had described the conditions as "horrendous" – and this week's weather was another challenge.

The game began in drizzle and ended in sweeping rain - the sort that, in shimmering floodlights, can look almost picturesque. Almost...

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But who notices a few drips down your neck when your team is winning? Borough supporters had returned deflated from Dartford, but by the second half of Tuesday's game they were pumped up and roaring again.

Postponed from an October Saturday because of Borough's FA Cup run, the visit of Dulwich Hamlet was just a little anti-climactic. The South London club and their buoyant supporters usually travel in numbers and liven up any game - but the logistics of a Tuesday night journey to the coast are trickier.

Hamlet's own league form has been patchy this season, but they always play without fear and they enjoy nothing better than a game which starts at high pace and then gets quicker.

That was precisely how Tuesday night's action began at the Lane. After two early chances for the Sports from corner-kicks, Hamlet snatched a surprise lead in the sixth minute, with a flicked finish by David Smith just beyond the reach of home keeper Lewis Carey.

The Sports were stirred rather than shaken - and a bit indignant. Chances came and went, but Dulwich were defending deep, and the home side were caught between playing their instinctive purist football or piling forward and getting the ball any which way into the Hamlet penalty area.

Indeed, the visitors were growing in confidence, and they created chances to extend the lead: one smart Lewis Carey save and two excellent interventions, by Max Sheaf and Freddie Carter, snuffed out the openings.

A huge home shout for a penalty was waved away by the referee - but the Sports were not relying on marginal decisions as they suddenly breached the Hamlet defences.

With 25 minutes played, a deep Josh Rees cross was met at the back post by Liam Nash - in his first full game back after injury - and Darren McQueen pounced to slide in the equaliser.

Most games have a turning point and that McQueen finish turned the mood for players, manager and huddled fans - from soaking wet gloom to a sudden sense of relief and optimism.

This Steve King squad is not perfect, but it has spirit, character, experience. And a drenching night at the Lane is no barrier. Within the next ten minutes, Borough had turned the match irreversibly in their favour with a 3-1 lead.

First, Rees pounded through from midfield, took a touch to get his angle right, and drilled past the visiting keeper for 2-1. The momentum had swung, and the belief was back.

And then it was Rees again - team skipper in every sense, and a man who embodies the spirit of drive and enterprise which his manager is demanding - who extended the lead to 3-1. Carter won the ball from Bangura following a Dulwich corner, and he drove forward with posse of four Borough players, before finding McQueen on the right.

The winger cut across to Rees, whose first effort was blocked before he tucked he ball past Sands at the second bite.

Hamlet really did not know what had hit them. From that bright start, they had seen the match ripped away from them.

The second half brought more of the same. In such buffeting conditions against unpredictable opponents, 3-1 was not necessarily a winning score. Hamlet were looking to sit deep and hit Borough on the counter - and they did exactly that with a swift end-to-end break for 3-2.

Anything Hamlet could do, Borough could do better. Liam Nash - in his first full game since a cheekbone injury - was the man on the mark. Kai Corbett brought down Sam Oguntayo's channel pass with ease, and he drove up the wing before crossing low. Paul McCallum dummied for Nash to steal his fifth goal of the season.

The last 20 minutes saw no further drama. Hamlet brought on the ageless Danny Mills, but even his scoring talents could not retrieve this game for the visitors.

#1915. Portugal boss Jorge Jesus claims Cristiano Ronaldo did NOT tell him he was retiring from international duty after fallout with superstar: 'I found out the same time as you'

Published: 16:01 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:09 EST, 6 November 2026

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insists he does not 'feel guilty' about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement and had no idea it was coming.

Ronaldo's explosive row with Jesus that escalated after he was left on the bench for a Nations League game and climaxed with the 41-year-old publishing a long statement hammering his manager, left their relationship in tatters.

And on Thursday, weeks after the dispute, Ronaldo announced his retirement from Portugal duty, bringing a sad end to his career on the international stage.

Jesus has now spoken for the first time about it, saying at a press conference: 'I don't feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision and, as such, his history cannot be ignored.

'I will never do that. Because he will always be a symbol, and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half. Sporting-wise, he has now made another decision, and I greatly respect his decision.'

When asked if he thought he was the reason for Ronaldo's retirement, the 72-year-old added: 'No... Maybe I rushed things, but not because of me. It was in his head that, with more or less call-ups, this was going to happen. It was always going to be during my tenure.

Jorge Jesus, pictured at a press conference on Friday, said he did not feel guilty about Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement

'I didn't speak to Ronaldo because I was thinking about calling him up. From that moment on, I was going to have time to talk to him.'

And Jesus insisted he had no idea why Ronaldo chose now to quit, adding: 'You have to ask him... The absolute certainty I have is that Cris worked with me for a year. We were happy at the club where we were, we were champions. I respect his decision at this moment.

'He would always have been with me throughout all these years that we were going to work together. He was the one who would decide. I don't know why he made that decision. What I do know is that he knew his time was coming, he was the one who would choose. And he chose. Only he can answer that better than I can.'

Ronaldo scored a world record 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal and won the 2016 European Championship as well as two Nations League titles.

But he will not add to those achievements now – instead stepping away after 23 years playing for his country.

In his retirement statement, he admitted that he had at times 'failed' and revealed that his decision was difficult, but felt proud of his work and willing to hand over the number seven jersey.

His final minutes in a Portugal shirt came against Wales in September, when he played 67 minutes in a 1-0 Nations League win over Wales.

After being left on the bench for their subsequent match against Norway, Ronaldo had a row with manager Jesus and flew away from Portugal's camp via his private jet.

Ronaldo never reached a World Cup final and cried after Portugal were knocked out by Spain in the last 16 over the summer

Marking his retirement, he wrote: 'To the people of Portugal, the day has come to return the number 7 jersey of our national team. I never felt it was exclusively mine. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility to wear it, to defend it, and to take it with me to stadiums all over the world.

'Today has come the moment to hand it over to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made just with the head, they are also made with the heart.

'I was always demanding of myself. I always wanted more, I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this jersey. There were perfect afternoons and nights, there were victories I will never forget.

'There were defeats that even today I find hard to remember. I also failed, I also suffered, there were also moments when I was not able to give the Portuguese people what they so desired. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.

'Throughout these years, I learned very simple things. Goals pass, trophies stay in museums, records end up being broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we occupy in people's hearts.

'If I ever made you happy, if ever a goal of mine made you hug someone, forget a problem, or simply feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also that. We suffer together, we get up together.

'If I got this far, it was because we were always hand in hand. And to the Portuguese, to all Portuguese people scattered around the world, I want to tell you one last thing. There is an image I will always carry with me: the moment the national anthem begins. I look around, I see my teammates, I see the stands, I see children, mothers, fathers, and grandfathers, I see Portuguese people who came from so far just to be there.

'And during those minutes, we stop being different. There are no clubs, there are no colors, there are no classes, there are no professions, there are no opinions. There is only one passion: Portugal.'

There will be questions over the way Ronaldo's international career has ended – to the public, it appears to be on rather bitter terms.

Ronaldo was livid after being left on the bench despite warming-up for Portugal's Nations League win over Norway on September 27 – the first time he has been an unused substitute during his 23-year international career.

The highlight of his Portugal career was lifting the 2016 European Championship, even if he got injured in the final

That led to him skipping three training sessions and abandoning the camp for Portugal's last two matches of the international break, fleeing to Spain via private jet.

He did not even watch their next match against Norway because he was soaring away on his plane with his family.

The former Manchester United star was vexed at how Jesus had handled his press conference after leaving him on the bench.

Ronaldo insisted that Jesus had broken a promise to apologise to the 'Portuguese people' and his team-mates for not bringing him on.

He claimed he had been guaranteed 30 minutes of football against Norway after the Portuguese FA persuaded him not to retire following the World Cup.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner even offered to retire if that was what the coach and head of Portuguese FA wanted, only for them to reiterate their desire to have him.

But most hurtfully, Ronaldo released a stinging 1,996-word statement accusing Jesus of 'broken promises'. He said the manager had agreed to deliver an eight-point mea culpa taking responsibility for leaving him on the bench after a supposed pact to play him.

Jesus did concede it was a mistake to make him warm up but gave a different narrative of events, saying: 'The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed.'

In the end, Ronaldo was fined £215 by the Portuguese FA and technically banned for a month – though that was backdated, making him free for their upcoming fixtures. But fans – and the man himself – will now have to embrace the next chapter as Portugal aim to move on without the most illustrious player in their history.

#1912. Darts on target – Sports aren’t: Eastbourne Borough beaten at Dartford

Although Liam Nash scored on his return to the Borough team, it proved no more than a consolation as Dan Smith, Max Fiddes and player-manager Ben Greenhalgh were all on target, with the full-time score 4-1 at Princes Park.

Steve King was forced to make changes as an unwell Freddie Carter and Arthur Grout were replaced by Harry Phipps and Paul McCallum. Nash was involved for the first time since September but was on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The hosts might have been ahead inside a minute had Lewis Carey not been alert. A corner from the right was sent to the far post where Ben Swift made contact and forced Carey to get down low and claw the ball off the line.

Josh Rees should actually have scored with the first Borough chance of note. McCallum managed to spray a pass into open space, where Darren McQueen raced to get in on goal. After being halted, he cut the ball back to Rees, 12 yards from goal, but he didn’t catch his effort well and the chance trickled into the hands of Dartford keeper Ryan Sandford.

They would rue that missed chance as the Darts went ahead on 15 minutes. After a long ball was sent upfield, Fiddes controlled superbly with an improvised flick before playing to strike partner Smith on the left, he jinked past Phipps before finding the far corner to give Dartford the lead.

Borough went in search of an immediate response as Kai Corbett’s cross was headed narrowly over by a Darts defender. Yet, just eleven minutes after the first goal, Dartford extended their lead via Fiddes. Smith turned provider, flicking the ball to Fiddes, who cut onto his left foot before producing a reversed finish into the far corner.

The game started to become end-to-end, but the Sports just could not hit the target. McQueen was unlucky to see his deflected effort strike the base of the post from the edge of the box, and McCallum could only head straight at Sandford.

Dartford made it three through player-manager Greenhalgh just after the half hour. Matthew Hayden made a mess of a clearance and it landed at Greenhalgh’s feet on the edge of the box, and he took a touch to set up a low drive past Carey.

Sandford was determined to keep a clean sheet against his former side as he made another fine stop to deny Rees. Max Sheaf’s cross from deep was pinpoint and met the head of an onrushing Rees. From just six yards, Rees thought he had pulled one back, but Sandford reacted sharply to parry out and behind.

It was the same old story just before half-time as another mistake allowed Fiddes to make it four. A poor pass led to a one-on-one opportunity with Fiddes against Hayden, and Dartford’s forward outmuscled Borough’s number two, before firing into the bottom corner.

The Sports looked for a response in the second 45 as they dominated possession against a stubborn Dartford block. They had to be patient for chances, but just felt it was not their day as they hit the woodwork again. Corbett’s free-kick panicked Sandford but smashed against the bar.

There was a consolation for Borough, and a fitting goal on his return for Nash. Fellow substitute Terrell Egbri’s cross was helped on by Shay Harrison towards Nash, and after miscuing a first attempt, he produced an instinctive scorpion kick into the roof of the net.

However, even with the momentum on their side, Borough couldn’t grab any more goals back.

#1911. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

#1907. Eastbourne United wallop Wick to keep league ambitions on track

A rare 4-3 home reversal against Roffey had not helped the mood, the near hurricane conditions rendering the match a spectacle rather than a competition.

On United went to Horsham YM last Tuesday. Sam Scott was suspended and Zach Robitaille made his full debut as United steamrollered hapless YM.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It could have been different; in a first half in which Alieu Secka only touched the ball from a couple of back passes, it was a solitary Ryan Blunt goal that separated the teams, and YM might be forgiven for thinking that it would be contained.

There was none of that as Anthony Storey’s half-time talk obviously did the trick. In a second half that once again they dominated, United added four more.

Blunt added a second with a left-foot drive before Callum Barlow rose at an impossible angle to head the third.

The YM keeper had earned his corn all match, and made an exceptional save from Ball before Blunt completed his hat-trick. Baran Kartal joined from the bench, and managed to sneak one home to make it 5-0, and to be fair, YM were fortunate that it was just five.

United knew that was more of a test coming on Saturday as they travelled to Wick.

Wick are having work done at Crabtree Park and are playing home games at Bognor’s Nyewood Lane ground. United were on a bit of a high and were unchanged but it was a very different start – as in the first minute at Hassocks, a defensive mix-up led to Wick taking the lead.

The difference here was that United bounced straight back. Joe Overy grabbed the first of his brace with eight minutes on the clock, and Wick were immediately looking more fragile. Overy and Jones were penetrating time and again, but without a real meaningful attempt.

Brett Patton, dominant as ever in midfield, took it upon himself to do the job, picking the ball up in the midfield, pushing straight through the defence and rounding the full-back like he wasn’t there, smashing home to make it 2-1. Patton does not score many, but when he does, it’s usually goal of the month.

Wick hearts were broken and it was an inevitable second half as United piled up the goal attempts. Blunt made it 3-1 just after the break before Overy’s excellent effort was pushed out by the keeper to Jorge Nones to sidefoot home from 12 yards.

The rout was completed minutes later as Overy scored his second, making it 5-2 before a raft of changes as surely the strongest bench in the league released Ball, Stone, James Hull, Gander and Kartal into the action.

The win meant United stayed a strong second in the table, and United have now scored 60 goals in their first 17 matches.

It’s a long campaign, but it’s not far off the halfway mark now, and United must be considered serious contenders for the league and certainly for the play-offs. Next up on Saturday it’s Little Common, so often a thorn in United’s side, at the Oval Arena.

#1906. 'He had options' - Key Leeds United figure explains decision to send Harry Gray to Sheffield Wednesday

Leeds United’s assistant sporting director Andrew Taylor has cited the expectation level at Sheffield Wednesday as a key reason behind the club’s decision to send Harry Gray there.

Gray is among Leeds’ most exciting prospects and has already represented England at various youth levels. A product of the famous Gray family and the younger brother of Tottenham Hotspur’s Archie, he made his senior Leeds debut against Stoke City in April 2025.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The versatile forward has since been exposed to EFL football via the loan system and spent the second half of last season with Rotherham United.

After suffering relegation from League One with the Millers, Gray was sent to third-tier promotion hopefuls Wednesday in the summer.

Taylor, formerly Leeds’ loan manager, told the club’s website: “Sheffield Wednesday are going to be strong.

“Secondly, there's a huge expectation on the club, a huge following, huge pressure because they're a massive club, and if we're trying to prepare him to come back and play for Leeds United in the Premier League, where there's huge expectation, huge following, huge pressure, it's really difficult to replicate that.

“Going somewhere like a Sheffield Wednesday under the scrutiny, under the big club mentality - everybody who plays against Sheffield Wednesday, it's their big game, so you've got to come up with solutions to win games, to be creative.”

Gray - somewhat unsurprisingly - attracted a host of admirers in the summer. He may have dropped out of League One with Rotherham but showed plenty of potential in a struggling team, registering three goals across 20 appearances.

Taylor explained: “He had options. He met with four teams, with the managers. One of my big philosophies is that the player has to have a big say in things, because he's the one going somewhere.

"Sheffield Wednesday is local enough; he's not going too far away, because when he first went out on loan to Rotherham United he was only 17 so there's a bit of a safeguarding issue. We don't want to send him somewhere too far because he can't just go and stay in a hotel on his own. So he gets to still stay at home until 18, and then obviously he can make his own decision.

"Last season he went to League One last year in a good club, but a struggling club, and he spent a lot of his time defending. I thought he had a really good loan spell last year, and there was a couple of possibilities of maybe the Championship this season, but we felt it might be the bottom end of the Championship. Our question was 'how do we go and give Harry Gray the best possible platform to go and be successful at what he's really good at, which is in the final third?'. A couple of other clubs we spoke to would have been in that category.”

Clubs sanction loan exits with the assumption their prospects will play regularly and while Leeds certainly hope Gray is an ever-present, Taylor does not think a battle for minutes is necessarily a bad thing.

He said: “There's going to be significant competition, and people maybe overlook this and say send him somewhere where he's going to play every minute of every game.

“Fine, but that's not the real world, because he comes back here or in a year or two years and Premier League squads are competitive. So actually, how about we send him somewhere where he can't just coast through the week, where he has to perform every day in training to make sure he's in the squad first and foremost on a Saturday, and then try and stay in the team? The only way you do that is by performing.”
