Beyond the words, Amorim wanted to understand, looking into the eyes of his players after the game, deeming them to be the reason for such a disappointing performance. Alphadjo Cisse, Ardon Jashari, Yunus Musah and the captain Adrien Rabiot are four specifically named.

The Portuguese pressed his players on why – after such an exhilarating victory as the derby – a display like that followed. As he explained post-match, the first topic the coach touched on was the approach.

From the opening minutes, the Rossoneri seemed at the mercy of the Hungarian’s pressing, incapable of finding solutions, ending the first half without a single shot on target. The team’s attitude wasn’t appreciated, nor that of some individuals.

Cisse, one of the key players in the start of the season and fresh from his first call-up to the national team, stood out only for his yellow card and was substituted at half-time, despite having played just a handful of minutes in the derby.

The Italian is barely 20 years old, and Amorim has already preemptively ‘pulled his ears’ to prevent him from getting too excited about his meteoric start. On Thursday, his substitution after 45 minutes said even more than the Portuguese coach’s post-match speech.

In the same boat as Cisse are Davide Bartesaghi, Filippo Terracciano, Jashari and Musah. Amorim is not necessarily pointing the finger exclusively at those who play less and started from the start against the Hungarians.

“The rotation has nothing to do with it,” the former Manchester United manager stated clearly in the press conference after the defeat. Also because, if the first half was a horror, the defeat was sealed in the second half when Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic came on.

Now all eyes immediately turn to the away match in Genoa, the last match before the international break. The topic wasn’t touched upon during Amorim’s meeting with the team at San Siro, but it’s clear that the whole thing was a prelude to an immediate reaction at the Ferraris.

#1827. Danny Kelly, journalist and talkSPORT presenter, dies aged 69 after cancer battle

Danny Kelly, a prominent journalist across music and sport, has died, at the age of 69, after a battle with cancer.

Kelly, a lifelong Tottenham fan, announced in March on talkSPORT - where he had worked for almost two decades - that he had been diagnosed with oesophageal cancer.

A music lover, Kelly spent time a editor of NME and, later, Q magazine. He joined talkSPORT in late 2007, and went on to host a number of the radio station’s programmes.

Kelly was most recently heard as host of The Athletic’s award-winning Tottenham podcast ‘The View From The Lane’.

A statement from talkSPORT, where he worked for almost two decades, read: “We are heartbroken to share that our much-loved friend and colleague Danny Kelly has died, aged 69.

“A cherished part of talkSPORT for so many years, Danny brought extraordinary wit, warmth and knowledge to our airwaves. His passion for football, music and life was infectious, and his kindness touched everyone around him.

Simon Jordan, former Crystal Palace owner, said on talkSPORT: "He was a brilliant broadcaster, editor, writer and friend, the reason I'm able to broadcast is because of Danny, it started with Danny, he nurtured me. He was an ideas factory. He fought this battle, the adversity he went through, the sadness, I feel choked, we thought Danny was coming through. He showed such strength and courage.

“We had such fun, during Covid we had such little material, nothing was going on, we had ideological debates, we disagreed, but we still created a dynamic between us, it’s stayed with me. I know him from years back. He will be missed, by those who knew him, the way he’d tell stories, strong views.”

However, it was clear the Premier League champions had ideally intended to bring in another proven talent in this area of the pitch after the club were gazumped by Chelsea in the race for Morgan Rogers.

#1825. Danny Murphy tells Liverpool to explore transfer move for £33m Man Utd target

Danny Murphy has urged Liverpool to strongly consider a transfer move for Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde this winter.

Liverpool invested heavily in the summer with a view to giving Andoni Iraola the best possible chance in the hot seat following Arne Slot’s dismissal as manager.

It saw Jeremy Jacquet, Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz all added to Iraola’s squad for a combined fee of around £200million – and the trio have gone on to enjoy encouraging starts to life at Anfield.

With the Reds having dropped points in five of their opening ten matches of the Premier League campaign, though, attentions have quickly turned to the January transfer window as an opportunity to further strengthen.

Milos Kerkez has blown hot and cold since joining Liverpool for a fee of £40million from Bournemouth 18 months ago and rumours have been circulating that the club could reenter the transfer market for a new left-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Merseyside giants have been credited with a strong interest in Juventus’ Andrea Cambiaso and Santos’ Vinicius Lira in recent days, with Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas both yet to fully convince fans that they could eventually fill the shoes left by Andy Robertson.

But according to Murphy, ‘super talent’ Balde could be the ideal signing for Liverpool given the out-of-favour Spaniard is already used to the expectations that come with playing for a ‘huge football club’.

Balde has made just three substitute appearances for Barca in La Liga this term and Manchester United have also been named as a potential escape route for the £33m-rated defender at the halfway point of the season.

‘I think Liverpool will be looking for a left-back but it’s hard because I don’t know Kerkez personally, I know he’s trying really hard and you can see it in his energy that he cares, and that’s a great start,’ the ex-Liverpool and England midfielder told Betarades.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He cares for the shirt and he’s working really hard to try and make it happen.

‘I think Balde could be great for Liverpool because he’s a super talent and he’s also got that experience of being at a huge football club with that expectation.

‘Balde’s a really good player. There’s lots of good players out there and Liverpool will be scouring the world.’

Murphy believes it could be time for Liverpool to look for ‘more established’ and ‘ready-made players’ after prioritising youth in recent transfer windows.

‘I think the most important thing is trying to bring somebody in who doesn’t make you guess whether he can deal with the pressure of a big club,’ he added.

‘It’s a delicate balance because Liverpool for years were very good at taking diamonds in from the rough, if you like. Someone like [Philippe] Coutinho, like [Andy] Robertson, like [Sadio] Mane even from Southampton. [Roberto] Firmino was about £20m.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool took those diamonds in the rough and moulded them into these superstars, and then when we’ve tried to go and spend massive money on these already made stars, it’s not quite worked.

‘I still think there are times, especially in defensive areas where you really do want ready-made players. Especially when you’re struggling.

‘I think Liverpool have got enough young players now who need to grow. I think now there’s an argument to have a few more players who are maybe a bit more established.’

Murphy has some sympathy for Kerkez but feels the Hungary international needs to get his head down and work on his composure if he is to make a success of his time at Liverpool.

‘He just lacks composure and quality in the final third when he gets there. Too often his final pass or his cross isn’t good enough,’ he continued.

‘He doesn’t have the composure of an Andy Robertson, and to be fair to him, you are filling the boots of arguably one of the best left-backs Liverpool’s ever had.”

‘I think the lack of quality at times is due to the fact he’s very fast. He’s very much 100 miles an hour. I’m surprised they’re not working with him more to slow him down in those areas and to just calm himself.

‘Now it wouldn’t be as bad if he was brilliant defensively, but he’s struggling defensively as well. His positional play is sometimes a bit off, he’s a bit erratic in terms of diving in or getting beat.

‘He likes jumping into people. It’s a dilemma for Liverpool, and I think one that they’ll definitely be looking at and trying to address, because not every signing works out.’

On Kerkez, Murphy went on: ‘I was somebody who saw him that year at Bournemouth and thought he looked like a terrific young player.

‘But the one thing that people don’t understand and it’s only when you’ve been in that position you can empathise with going from playing in one environment to being in the intense, magnified world of Liverpool Football Club.

‘Every game, every minute, every mistake is analysed by the fans, by the press, by the worldwide audience, and I think that expectation, and that pressure is a bit much for him.’

So far, so good. When you run a football club as badly as INEOS have done, thick skin is essential.

Football reporter Matt Verri has given his blunt thoughts on Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s reign.

Reunions with Harry Kane and Cole Palmer? A long-term replacement for Bruno Fernandes?

The Glazer family will reportedly attend Wednesday’s meeting in Monaco, where Michael Carrick’s dismissal is expected to be ratified.

Carrick is still at the club’s Carrington training ground to oversee training, while discussions with potential successor Mauricio Pochettino are accelerating.

Michael Carrick is back at Manchester United’s training ground today, as club executives set to discuss his future at a meeting in Monaco.

Huge breaking news out of The Athletic, who report that Manchester United are reportedly finalising an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach.

Mauricio Pochettino is the the Glazer family’s preferred choice to be the next Manchester United manager.

Carrick is expected to leave the club in the coming days after overseeing just one win in United’s opening 10 league matches. The club would then be searching for its third permanent manager in three years.

Pochettino has previously been interviewed for the role in 2018 and 2022, but was overlooked in favour of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Erik ten Hag.

However, his reputation in the United States has grown since taking charge of the national team two years ago, and The i Paper report that the Glazers believe the club should not pass up the opportunity to appoint him again.

Michael Carrick lives to fight another day, as his future is decided in Monaco, not Manchester, today.

Chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have flown out to meet co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who has a home in the principality and company INEOS have offices there.

Carrick is expected to again take charge of a depleted first-team training session at Carrington today.

Antonio Conte will not become the new Manchester United manager.

That is according to Fabrizio Romano, who reports that the speculation around the former Chelsea and Tottenham head coach moving to Old Trafford has “gone cold”.

The Italian had been heavily linked with a switch to the north west in recent weeks as pressure piled on Michael Carrick after a dismal run of form saw the Red Devils win just once in 11 matches, as they lie in the relegation zone of the Premier League table.

Zubimendi joined Arsenal in a £60 million deal from Real Sociedad last year and played an integral role in his first season at the club as Mikel Arteta’s side won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final.

So far this season, Zubimendi is yet to start in 10 Premier League games and is facing increased competition for a place in midfield following Arsenal’s decision to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United in the summer.

Both Chelsea and Atletico Madrid have been linked with a move for Zubimendi, and his Spain teammate, Alex Baena, said this week that the Arsenal midfielder would be a ‘great addition’ to the Spanish club.

However, Spanish reporter Antonio Ruiz told El Partidazo de COPE on Tuesday night that Atletico have ruled themselves out of the race to sign Zubimendi in January.

#1822. Who Manchester United stars 'want' to replace Michael Carrick - and it’s not Mauricio Pochettino

Michael Carrick has been pictured arriving at Carrington, potentially for the last time as Manchester United manager, before he is likely to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, though reports claim that some players want Unai Emery.

It was business as usual for the under-fire Carrick on Wednesday morning as he arrived at Man Utd’s AON Complex in order to take training with the players who are not currently away on international duty.

However, it is expected that the decision to sack Carrick will be made later today some 800 miles away in Monaco, where chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are travelling to hold a meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls the sporting operation at the club.

It is understood that while no final decision has yet been made, Berrada and Wilcox are likely to recommend to Ratcliffe that a change is needed in an attempt to turn around United’s dismal run of form that has left them sitting in the Premier League relegation zone with one win from 10 games.

United’s majority owners the Glazers will also reportedly be part of that meeting, which is said to have been pre-planned and part of regular talks between the club hierarchy to discuss strategy. Ratcliffe has a home in Monaco, where his company INEOS also have offices.

It was widely reported on Wednesday morning that United were in the process of finalising a deal with Pochettino in the event that they part ways with Carrick, with personal terms close to being agreed.

Former Tottenham, Chelsea, Paris Saint-Germain and Southampton boss Pochettino is currently the head coach of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and only signed a new contract through the 2030 World Cup back in August, after leading the USA to the World Cup last 16 on home soil in the summer.

However, there is a clause included in that deal that would allow United to release him from it early for a fee of $10million (£7.5m). The USA have a crucial two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti coming up, with the first game in Miami on Saturday.

Ex-Newcastle manager Eddie Howe had also been thought to be a favoured candidate to replace Carrick after reportedly turning down an approach from Crystal Palace, along with former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann.

Antonio Conte had also been linked with the post, along with Aston Villa’s Emery and Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler.

talkSPORT claim that United’s senior stars expect Carrick to be sacked and Pochettino to become their new manager, marking his first return to the Premier League since an ill-fated one-season spell at Chelsea in 2023/24.

However, the same report says that some United players were hoping for the appointment of Emery, who is set to sign a new long-term contract extension at Villa Park instead.

#1819. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:07 EST, 7 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

#1818. Chelsea news: Dermot Gallagher backs double Blues VAR snub versus Sunderland

By Darren Plant | 09 Nov 2026 13:02

Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher has backed VAR over the decisions that went against Chelsea during Sunday's game at Sunderland.

The Black Cats recorded a deserved 1-0 victory courtesy of Enzo Le Fee's first-half penalty at the Stadium of Light.

However, the decision to award Sunderland a spot kick has been questioned, with replays suggesting that Brian Brobbey fouled Levi Colwill prior to being brought down in the penalty area.

Meanwhile, Cole Palmer could have arguably won a spot kick for Chelsea at the other end having been upended by a combination of Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka.

Xabi Alonso's side were not given the decision because any infringement was deemed to have started or taken place outside of the penalty area.

Speaking on 'Ref Watch' on Sky Sports News, Gallagher claimed that Colwill could have no complaints over the Sunderland penalty decision.

He said: "They are both grabbing. It starts outside the area, the referee does not take sides, but once Brobbey gets in front of him and Colwill does bot let go, that is when he falls foul of the penalty.

"Once he is in front, he is in the ascendancy and Colwill drags him to the ground, so I think penalty."

When asked on the process involving Palmer, O'Nien and Ahoka, Gallagher added: "The referee gives a foul. That is what he gives.

"O'Nien completes the action when he is in the box. Once he gives the first foul, that is it. What happens afterwards, he can only take action if he deems there is serious foul play.

"That is what he fed back. What he has to do is, when he is talking to VAR, he has to say who he thinks is the player [committing the foul].

"It is O'Nien's boot in the penalty area. The argument is that if he is on the line, it is a penalty. But it is O'Nien's boot; you can't see the ball.

"O'Nien goes second. VAR said Ahoka went first and he is the first offender. They didn't stop the game. The game went on."

Alonso refused to criticise the officials in his post-match press conference, instead choosing to focus on the poor performance from his team.

However, during the match, the Spaniard appeared furious about Sunderland going unpunished over the Palmer incident.

#1817. England XI vs Croatia: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Nations League

Dan Burn and James Hill have been added to the England squad as replacements for Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa ahead of Thursday’s match against Croatia.

The Three Lions face Croatia at Wembley Stadium in their penultimate Nations League group game, before completing their group-phase in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday.

Manchester City centre-back Guehi was assessed over the weekend after being substituted with a hip injury at half time of their defeat to Nottingham Forest but has now pulled out of the squad.

In his place, Thomas Tuchel called up the 34-year-old Newcastle defender. He had said on Friday that “difficult phone calls” had been had with Burn, Dean Henderson and Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson when leaving them behind. But the former is now in as Guehi’s replacement.

Meanwhile, it was announced on Tuesday morning that Konsa will not be available for the Croatia game, but is expected to return to full training later in the week ahead of the Spain fixture. He has already joined up with England and was following his own individualised training programme while the rest of the squad trained at Tottenham on Wednesday afternoon.

The other omission from training on Wednesday was Inter Milan’s Djed Spence, is now a doubt for the Croatia match. Spence, despite being right-footed, is in the squad as a left-back.

As such, Tuchel must decide whether to hand Hill a senior debut or reshuffle his defence with Ben White coming in at right-back, thus allowing Jarell Quansah to partner Burn in the middle.

Captain Harry Kane is expected to start and will overtake Peter Shilton to become England’s all-time most-capped player.

Arsenal duo Bukayo Saka (injury) and Noni Madueke (selection decision) are not in the squad this month but the head coach has explained that he sees his options on the right wing as being Liverpool’s Rio Ngumoha, Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, Nottingham Forest’s Morgan Gibbs-White and Fulham’s Josh King.

Declan Rice is back in the mix and available after missing the last international break due to load management.

Jobe Bellingham of Borussia Dortmund, brother of Real Madrid’s Jude, is in the squad for the very first time at senior level. He, King and the Brighton veteran goalkeeper Jason Steele are the only uncapped players among Tuchel’s squad.

#1816. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1815. Man United head coach Michael Carrick defends Diogo Dalot amid fierce criticism of struggling defender

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 13:16, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 13:18

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has defended Diogo Dalot amid the latest round of fierce criticism of the Portugal international.

Dalot has often played out of position at left-back this season, and it has been a tough campaign for the 27-year-old, who has been a part of a defence that has struggled badly this term.

The full-back was substituted in the second half of Sunday's game with Aston Villa, and his withdrawal proved to be a popular decision with the Man United fans.

A number of Red Devils supporters revealed their displeasure at Dalot's performance when he was removed in the 66th minute.

Dalot gave away a penalty against Villa and was arguably at fault for the first goal that Man United conceded during what was a chaotic Premier League fixture.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Dalot's future, with the Portuguese potentially leaving Old Trafford during this summer's transfer window.

However, Carrick has come to the defence of the full-back.

“We've got to be careful with that, I think. I understand the frustration. I understand the disappointment of the supporters, so I get it. We're all frustrated. We're all disappointed. And the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that," Carrick told reporters.

"Diogo gives absolutely everything. He's played in different positions. He's played left-back. He's played really well at times. He gives a penalty away today. That's, you know… he knows that.

"Maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that's part of it, he's made a mistake. But he cares an awful lot, and he's given everything. So I like what he brings to the team.

"I like what he brings to the group. I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we've got. Picking the team and who plays the next game, that's a whole different decision. But it's a whole different game that we've got to look forward to now.”

The Portugal international has represented Man United on 260 occasions since arriving from Porto in 2018, scoring 10 goals and registering 20 assists, and he has featured 14 times in all competitions during the 2026-27 campaign.

Dalot has a contract at Man United until June 2028, with the option of a further year, but both parties need to cut ties during next summer's transfer window.

The Red Devils could sign as many as four new defenders in 2027, and Dalot will not be short of interest, with the likes of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter Milan all thought to be keen.

#1814. Milan Primavera 5-1 AlbinoLeffe: Vincent Ibrahimovic scores twice in second consecutive rout

On a day in which Milan’s first team, Futuro and Primavera sides all play, things have started on the right note.

After a tough run of recent results in the league, the Primavera managed to build on their mid-week cup win with a strong performance against last weekend Monza, winning 5-0 away from home. Max Anastasio, Mattia Zaramella (x2), Riccardo Grassini and Yanis Messaoudi scored in that rout.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

So, returning home to the PUMA House of Football, the challenge was to build on that result. The response was resounding: Giovanni Renna’s side won 5-1 against AlbinoLeffe in the early kick-off.

Milan took the lead after five minutes with a fine goal from Balentien, and the second goal came in the tenth minute through Vincent Ibrahimovic, who capitalized on a defensive error.

The visitors pulled one back in the 30th minute through Gamba, but in the 36th minute the Rossoneri reopened their two-goal advantage as Ibrahimovic got his name on the scoresheet again, curling one around the goalkeeper from inside the box.

In the second half, Anastasio scored the fourth goal on the hour mark following a cross from Angelicchio, and in the 68th minute Zaramella sealed the deal with an easy one-on-one with the goalkeeper.

The win puts Milan in sixth place in the table on 16 points, and they are now just five points off Parma in top spot, and three behind both Roma and Inter who occupy second and third at the moment. Next up is a trip to face Lazio after the break, the team currently in the place above them.

#1813. Kane, Palmer and Paz: Mauricio Pochettino’s dream Manchester United XI revealed

Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly gearing up to become the new Manchester United manager, as club chiefs meet in Monaco to discuss Michael Carrick’s future.

A new face in the dugout is needed with the club currently languishing in the relegation zone after the worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Pochettino will be expected to be backed in the transfer window, both in January and moving forward, as Man Utd bid to get back to their glorious days of the past.

That would mean yet more serious investment in the squad, but what exactly would a Pochettino dream XI look like at United?

Senne Lammens may have thrown a few into his own net recently, but he is still a good goalkeeper and a relatively recent recruit. If it ain’t (totally) broke, don’t fix it.

Full-back has become a real problem for Man Utd. Luke Shaw’s poor injury record continues to affect both his fitness and form, and Diogo Dalot is clearly not up to the task despite being in his ninth season at Old Trafford.

At Tottenham particularly, Pochettino worked wonders with impressive and robust young full-backs, who grew into the league’s best under his tutelage. That brings Lewis Hall - even with a new contract - and Spurs’s Archie Gray into view.

Whether they would join Man Utd is another matter, but working with Pochettino would surely be an attractive pull. Hall and Gray have years ahead of them, but are also assured Premier League performers who are well-balanced between attack and defence. And in Gray, there are burgeoning leadership skills, too.

At centre-back, you could just imagine the Argentina connection bringing Lisandro Martinez back into scope for Man Utd’s medium-term future, and Pochettino has always relished the challenge of working with high-ceiling young players. Leny Yoro, still only 20, is certainly that.

Central midfield would be a mix of youth and experience, with Youri Tielemans taking the lead and Kobbie Mainoo learning alongside him. Meanwhile, a reunion with Chelsea’s Cole Palmer — who played by far his best football in blue during Pochettino’s tenure — would be a mouthwatering prospect.

#1812. Sir Jim Ratcliffe should be ashamed at how he is running Manchester United and treating Michael Carrick

“Best in class”? You’ve got to be joking, Jim. INEOS’s running of Man Utd has been a calamitous mess

As the latest Manchester United embarrassment meanders towards an inevitable conclusion, Sir Jim Ratcliffe can comfort himself in the knowledge that he has got some things right.

In an interview with BBC Sport last year, Ratcliffe admitted: “I recognise I’m unpopular at the moment. I’m prepared to be and can deal with being unpopular for a period of time.”

So far, so good. When you run a football club as badly as INEOS have done, thick skin is essential.

“Manchester United has come off the rails and we need to get it back on the rails,” Ratcliffe continued. Again, all correct for now.

“I believe that what we’re doing will put it back on the rails and we’ll finish up being where Liverpool or Real Madrid are today.”

For all this shambolic process has been entirely in keeping with how the club’s hierarchy operate, it is a shameful way to treat Carrick

Try not to laugh. Fast forward a year and United are spending the November international break in the relegation zone. It is their lowest position in the league after ten matches for 40 years.

It was INEOS who put forward Mission 21, the plan to deliver United a 21st league title by 2028 to mark the club’s 150th anniversary. Would winning the Championship count?

United fans need not worry, though. The good news is that the club is in safe hands. In 2024, Ratcliffe declared: “We need to populate all the key roles with people who are best in class. 10-out-of-10s.”

Step forward Omar Berrada, chief executive, and director of football Jason Wilcox. The brains trust are in Monaco for a meeting with Ratcliffe on Wednesday to discuss the club’s strategy and more specifically the future of Michael Carrick.

Except we already know the outcome because it leaked two days earlier. Berrada and Wilcox will recommend that Carrick is sacked as United embark on a mid-season manager search for the third year in a row.

For all this shambolic process has been entirely in keeping with how the club’s hierarchy operate, it is a shameful way to treat Carrick.

Sacking him is not the wrong decision. United have one league win all season and are a dream to play against. The squad is not good enough but results have still been abysmal under Carrick, who has showed no sign of turning things around.

However, that does not excuse how the situation has been handled. The 45-year-old made 464 appearances for the club. He won five Premier League titles at Old Trafford. While the fans have rightly aimed their fury at the players and the board in recent weeks, Carrick has retained their support.

And yet the incompetence of United’s leadership meant that he spent Tuesday at the club’s training ground, pretending it was business as usual despite knowing he would imminently be sacked.

The delay is said to be because Wilcox and Berrada want to inform Carrick face-to-face, but only after they consulted with Ratcliffe. That, of course, can only be done in person in Monaco and after waiting a couple of days for good measure. Add video calls to the list of things beyond this trio.

It is a laughable attempt at claiming to do things the right way, with the sacking decision effectively having already been made public.

This is a rudderless ship with no hope of success under the current leadership

To undermine that stance further, United are in talks with Mauricio Pochettino. Discussions are believed to be in the final stages and an agreement is close. All while Carrick remains in charge and shuffles papers at the training ground.

Nor is it any great surprise. Ratcliffe oversaw the Erik ten Hag debacle in 2024, when the club were set to sack the Dutchman and spoke to several replacements, only to then panic and give him a contract extension. Ten Hag was sacked a few months later.

Dan Ashworth stuck his head in for five months to the cost of £4.1million. It took 16 months to work out Sir Dave Brailsford knew nothing about football. Wilcox was involved in the appointment of back-three zealot Ruben Amorim and then forcefully suggested to the manager he might want to not play a back-three. Amorim was gone days later.

Back to Ratcliffe and his prophetic words. “They made a complete cock-up of it, shocking really,” he told The Times last year, when asked about the club’s previous leadership under the Glazers.

“The first management group, they thought they understood and wanted to get involved in buying footballers but they didn’t have the knowledge to buy footballers. They went in the marketplace, spraying money around and it was just random, wasn’t it?”

Fortunately Ratcliffe had the “best in class” to correct that. Wilcox oversaw the summer window and had the clever plan of caring about only one position. No more randomness. This squad would be rebuilt in instalments, starting in midfield.

Forget that the defence was in dire need of reinforcements. Or that the midfield overhaul did not involve signing an elite midfielder. Or that no serious club has ever operated in that way.

That was the support Carrick was given, having led United back into the Champions League. Hopefully Pochettino will have his say in the defenders that arrive next summer. Perhaps the next manager after him will be allowed a forward signing or two.

It is absurd that Wilcox will come away from the Monaco summit with another manager gone and his job still intact. But then Ratcliffe has backed himself into a corner, having stuck with Wilcox through all the mistakes of the past two years.

Sack Wilcox and admit a failure of leadership in putting the wrong man in place? Or keep Wilcox and in doing so admit the “best in class” soundbite was just that, confirming this is a rudderless ship with no hope of success under the current leadership?

For now, it will be the easy decision. Remove another manager and start the cycle again. From Ratcliffe at the top to Wilcox and Berrada below him, all the way down to the players on the pitch, United have individuals out of their depth at every level.

Carrick has clearly not delivered this season either but the disrespect in the final hours of his reign is further evidence that he is better off out of this mess.

#1811. Chelsea, Man City, PSG among clubs chasing £25m defender labelled the ‘next Raphael Varane’

By Oliver Thomas | 09 Nov 2026 13:19

European giants Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and Manchester City are reportedly among a big list of clubs chasing Lens defender Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou.

Reigning Champions League winners PSG already have a wealth of defensive options at their disposal, but finding a long-term successor to captain Marquinhos, 32, may soon become a priority, prompting the club to keep a close eye on France's brightest emerging talents.

Chelsea and Man City, meanwhile, have both had their fair share of defensive issues this season, conceding 29 goals combined after 10 Premier League games, and may also consider delving into the market for backline reinforcements.

According to TEAMtalk, Chelsea owners BlueCo and City Football Group, the parent company of Man City, have been keeping tabs on 21-year-old Ganiou, while PSG are ‘fully aware’ of his potential.

Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United, Brentford and Fulham are said to be among the other English clubs to have watched the highly-rated centre-back this calendar year.

Ligue 1 duo Marseille and Monaco are also monitoring Ganiou progress, with Italian clubs Atalanta BC and Como, and Bundesliga pair Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig among the other European teams keeping a close eye on his development.

Ganiou has enhanced his reputation with Lens following a breakthrough period in French football, making his Ligue 1 debut in October 2025.

Widely regarded as Lens’ greatest-ever academy product, Ganiou is a physical, pacey and elegant centre-back who has been compared to former France and Real Madrid defender Raphael Varane.

The young defender's path to the first team was somewhat unconventional, involving temporary stints away from Lens at Annecy and Padova to bypass strict loan registration rules.

However, following his successful return, Ganiou made a massive impression during his debut season with Lens last season, with his rapid breakthrough convincing the club's hierarchy to reward him with a four-year contract extension over the summer.

Ganiou has made a total of 37 senior appearances for Lens in all competitions, with 29 of those coming in a memorable 2025-26 campaign that saw Les Sang et Or finish second in Ligue 1 and win the Coupe de France for the first time in the club's history.

The 6ft 1in defender worked under current Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage last season and has since established himself as a first-team regular, despite the early departure of Dino Toppmoller and arrival of Yannick Cahuzac as the club’s new head coach in September.

Valued at €30m (£25m) by transfermarkt and capped five times by France Under-21s, Ganiou is currently sidelined with a knee injury, but he hopes to be back in the first-team fold soon and continue his impressive trajectory as a core component of the Lens defence while interested suitors continue to watch on.

#1810. 'I want to win the Ballon d'Or': JJ Gabriel sets out his lofty ambitions as Man United wonderkid, 16, closes in on move to Real Madrid after quitting Red Devils

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:08 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 06:09 EST, 7 November 2026

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he dropped the clearest hint yet that he is heading to Real Madrid in an interview with Spanish media.

The 16-year-old sensation stunned Manchester United with a formal transfer request in September and is now on the verge of finalising his move to the Spanish capital.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet last month, with Gabriel now having secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage.

The youngster, who is currently working with a personal trainer in Madrid, practically confirmed the transfer in an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca on Friday night, admitting he had a clear preference to Real over archrivals Barcelona.

'Obviously Madrid,' Gabriel told the outlet when asked which LaLiga giant he preferred.

According to the newspaper, who expects his move to be finalised in January, Gabriel's response prompted a laugh from his father and mentor Joe O'Cearuill.

Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel poses for his interview with Spanish newspaper Marca

Gabriel is set to complete a move to Real Madrid after formally requesting to leave Old Trafford

'My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,' explained the talented youngster, who scored a hat-trick for Manchester United in the UEFA Youth League just days before submitting his transfer request.

Although Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal narrowly missed out on winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or - which was held aloft by England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane - the two LaLiga giants have long had a rich association with the award, regularly producing the world's best footballer.

While sources at United insist there has been no club-to-club contact, it appears only a matter of time before Gabriel is sporting Real Madrid's iconic all-white jersey.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

The prodigy, who was 14 when he netted twice on his debut, has also played - and scored - for Manchester United's Under-21 side.

The Red Devils were rocked in September when Gabriel and his representatives made a bombshell request to have his academy contract torn up. That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

Gabriel's dream is to win the Ballon d'Or, which was awarded this year to England's Harry Kane

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson has been the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

His father has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent and is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

#1808. Man City transfer news: Etihad player ‘finished’ under Enzo Maresca with January plans revealed

By Oliver Thomas | 09 Nov 2026 13:56

Manchester City defender Rayan Ait-Nouri is reportedly ‘finished’ at the Etihad Stadium having fallen down the pecking order under manager Enzo Maresca.

Ait-Nouri was signed by Maresca’s predecessor Pep Guardiola in the summer of 2025, joining from Wolverhampton Wanderers in a £31m deal and penning a five-year contract.

The 25-year-old left-back chipped in with five assists in 28 appearances for City across all competitions last season, missing the majority of December and January following his involvement with Algeria at the Africa Cup of Nations.

Ait-Nouri celebrated winning both the FA Cup and EFL Cup in his debut campaign with the Sky Blues, though he did not feature in either final played at Wembley.

This term, Ait-Nouri has struggled to force his way into Maresca’s first-team plans and is currently viewed as a third-choice left-back behind Josko Gvardiol and Nico O'Reilly.

Ait-Nouri is yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Man City in 2026-27, while he has made just two substitute appearances in the Champions League – his only two starts have come in the EFL Cup.

Although Ait-Nouri is said to remain keen to fight for his place at Man City, Football Insider claims that the defender has failed to make an impression under Maresca.

The report adds that Ait-Nouri is unlikely to play ahead of either Gvardiol or O’Reilly any time soon, and could therefore push for a move away from City during the January transfer window in search of regular first-team football.

Maresca recently admitted that Ait-Nouri is struggling for game time, telling reporters: "He's a clear full-back. In that position, we have [Gvardiol], who is doing fantastic, we have [O'Reilly], who when he is fit is doing fantastic; and he's the same position, so it's just competition between them."

A surprise transfer to City’s rivals Manchester United was mooted for Ait-Nouri in the closing stages of the summer window, and the possibility of the Red Devils making a January swoop is said to have been explored.

While agreeing personal terms would seemingly not be an issue for Ait-Nouri, who could be receptive to a switch across Manchester, it is understood that the relationship between City and United is the ‘main issue’ that could scupper this potential move.

Serie A giants Juventus have also been consistently linked with a move for Ait-Nouri and a switch to Italy is thought to be more realistic at this stage, though the Old Lady may prefer to negotiate an initial loan deal.

#1805. The five Premier League managers under the most pressure - where does Michael Carrick rank?

By Joshua Cole | 09 Nov 2026 15:42

The November international break has arrived at a particularly uncomfortable time for several Premier League managers, with the opening months of the 2026-27 campaign exposing serious problems at clubs with very different expectations and ambitions.

While some teams have made encouraging progress, others have struggled to deliver consistent results, leaving their managers facing growing questions about their futures as club executives consider whether a change in the dugout could improve their fortunes.

Manchester United's Michael Carrick remains among the most vulnerable after another difficult start to the season, while Crystal Palace's Pierre Sage is reportedly on the brink of losing his position following Sunday's defeat to Liverpool.

Regis Le Bris, Matthias Jaissle and Oliver Glasner also entered the weekend under scrutiny, although their respective results have altered the immediate picture, with Sunderland and Nottingham Forest recording important victories against Chelsea and Manchester City.

With the Premier League now pausing for international football, Sports Mole looks at five managers who have had plenty to think about over the coming weeks.

Carrick's position at Manchester United remains one of the biggest talking points in the Premier League, with the former midfielder struggling to convince that he is the right person to lead the club out of its current difficulties.

United have endured a miserable opening to the campaign, with their 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday leaving them 18th in the table with just eight points from 10 matches.

Although rescuing a point after falling behind was evidence of some fighting spirit, the result extended their disappointing league run, with Carrick still waiting for his first Premier League victory since August.

The situation has been particularly concerning given United's status and the resources available to the manager, while their 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth and subsequent 2-0 loss against Chelsea have intensified scrutiny of his tactical approach and ability to get the best out of his squad.

Carrick retains considerable support among sections of the fanbase, which could work in his favour, but the club's hierarchy will be increasingly concerned about United's position in the relegation zone and the prospect of allowing the season to deteriorate further.

The Red Devils' dramatic comeback against Roma in the Champions League offered some encouragement, although the Premier League remains the priority, and the international break could provide United's decision-makers with an opportunity to assess whether he deserves more time.

Sage appears to be facing the most immediate threat of the five managers, with Crystal Palace reportedly preparing to part company with the Frenchman following their disappointing start to the season.

Appointed in the summer as Oliver Glasner's successor, Sage has struggled to reproduce the organisation and consistency that made Palace an established force under the Austrian.

Sunday's 3-1 defeat to Liverpool at Selhurst Park left the Eagles bottom of the Premier League table with seven points from their opening 10 matches, having recorded just two victories during that period.

Their defensive problems have been particularly damaging, with Palace conceding 24 goals, the highest total in the division, while their inability to turn performances into positive results has placed considerable pressure on their new manager.

The Frenchman's position has also been weakened by a lack of support from sections of the Palace fanbase, with the 5-0 defeat against Brighton earlier in the campaign providing another difficult moment during his short tenure.

According to reports, the club are now preparing to dismiss Sage, with the international break offering a convenient opportunity to make a managerial change without immediately disrupting the playing schedule.

Having inherited a difficult situation following the departure of Glasner and the loss of important players, Sage can point to mitigating circumstances, but the results have been insufficient to convince the hierarchy that he can turn things around.

Le Bris has earned considerable credit for his work at Sunderland, having guided the Black Cats to promotion before overseeing an impressive seventh-place finish in their first Premier League season back in the top flight.

However, expectations have changed following that achievement, and the Frenchman has discovered that maintaining Sunderland's progress is proving considerably more difficult.

The Black Cats entered the weekend in the relegation zone, with their performances and results raising questions about whether the squad had been strengthened sufficiently to cope with the demands of another campaign.

A 2-0 Europa League defeat to Dinamo Zagreb had also increased the pressure, particularly after Le Bris admitted that his decision to rotate the team had not worked as intended.

Nevertheless, Sunderland produced an important response on Sunday, beating Chelsea 1-0 to move up to 19th with eight points.

The victory should ease some of the immediate scrutiny surrounding Le Bris, although it does little to disguise the broader problems facing the club, particularly with a demanding run of fixtures awaiting them after the international break.

The manager's previous achievements should earn him patience, but Sunderland need to demonstrate that they can compete consistently rather than relying on occasional victories to keep their survival hopes alive.

Jaissle's position at Newcastle United is not necessarily as precarious as those of Carrick and Sage, but there are growing concerns about the direction of a club that expected to challenge for European qualification.

The German inherited a difficult situation following Eddie Howe's departure, particularly after Newcastle sanctioned the sales of several influential players, including Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes across successive transfer windows.

However, the significant investment made in replacements has not produced the expected improvement, with Newcastle struggling to establish a consistent playing identity under their new manager.

Their 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday left them 12th with 12 points from 10 matches, continuing a disappointing run that has included damaging defeats and unconvincing performances.

Jaissle has also faced criticism for Newcastle's approach in possession, with his explanation following the defeat to Everton that his players had resorted to too many long balls raising further questions about the team's tactical execution.

There are mitigating circumstances, particularly the scale of the squad changes and the limited time available to build a cohesive team, but Newcastle's underlying performances have offered little encouragement.

The international break gives Jaissle an opportunity to work on those problems, although a significant improvement will be required if he is to convince supporters and the club's hierarchy that he is capable of taking Newcastle forward.

Glasner's situation is an interesting one because, despite facing considerable pressure before the weekend, the Austrian has given himself some breathing space with an impressive victory over Manchester City.

Forest had endured a difficult opening to the campaign, with their lack of goals and inability to turn promising performances into victories leaving them 19th after nine matches.

Their attacking struggles were particularly concerning, although the underlying statistics suggested that Glasner's side had been unfortunate, with their expected points tally significantly better than their actual position.

The club's ownership structure also makes the situation uncomfortable for the manager, with Evangelos Marinakis having demonstrated little hesitation in making managerial changes when results have failed to meet expectations.

However, Forest delivered one of the weekend's biggest surprises by beating Manchester City 3-1 at the City Ground, with the result lifting them to 16th in the table on nine points.

The victory represents a significant boost for Glasner, particularly after a period in which questions were being raised about his team's attacking efficiency and ability to collect points.

Nevertheless, one impressive result will not completely resolve Forest's problems, and the Austrian will need to build on the performance when domestic football resumes.

With the club's ambitions and expectations remaining high, Glasner will know that continued improvement is essential if he is to avoid becoming the next managerial casualty in an increasingly unforgiving Premier League.

#1804. How Thomas Frank could raid Tottenham in Crystal Palace transfer spree

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Thomas Frank is the frontrunner to take over from Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager.

The Dane has been out of work since stepping away from football following his departure from Tottenham in February.

Frank was on Palace’s shortlist over the summer as they looked for a replacement for Oliver Glasner, but they instead opted to bring in Sage following a successful spell with Ligue 1 side Lens.

Just 10 games into the new season, though, Sage is expected to leave Palace with the club rock bottom of the Premier League table heading into the international break.

A succession plan is already under way, with Frank at the top of a long list of potential candidates to take over at Selhurst Park.

Despite a disastrous eight-month period at Spurs - leaving the club sitting just above the relegation zone - Frank is still well regarded from his time at Brentford and is viewed as an experienced Premier League operator.

Should Frank take charge at Palace, he will likely need reinforcements in January and could look to raid his former club to steer the Eagles away from the relegation zone.

With that in mind, Standard Sport has identified three Spurs players Palace could look at if Frank takes the reins.

Brought in from Atletico Madrid last January as Frank desperately looked to bolster his midfield options after Rodrigo Bentancur underwent hamstring surgery, Gallagher’s return to the Premier League has not gone quite as well as he would have hoped.

The former Chelsea man chose Spurs over Aston Villa not only because of a desire to return to London and a healthy wage packet but also to put himself in contention for England’s World Cup squad.

Instead, the midfielder became embroiled in a messy relegation battle and was, for a period, a lightning rod for criticism due to his limited capabilities in possession.

Gallagher played an important role for Roberto De Zerbi towards the end of last season but has seen his minutes limited this term following the arrivals of Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

A return to Palace, where he enjoyed arguably his most productive season as a professional on loan from Chelsea in 2021/22, would make sense for both parties.

Spurs, though, are said to be reluctant to part ways with the 26-year-old.

Another player Spurs would ideally want to keep hold of is centre-back Marcos Senesi, who only joined the club in the summer on a free transfer from Bournemouth.

De Zerbi was keen to bring Senesi to north London because of his ability to play out from the back, but the Argentine has so far seen his minutes restricted with Dutch duo Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke Spurs’ first-choice centre-back pairing.

Senesi is a good tactical fit and provides important cover for Spurs, but his desire to play regularly could be tested if Palace come in with an offer when the January window opens.

Palace have not suitably replaced Maxence Lacroix or Marc Guehi, so a new centre-back would likely be a priority for Frank, who instigated Spurs’ initial interest in Senesi.

Spurs’ top goalscorer last season has been banished from the first team after failing to force a move away from the club over the summer.

The Brazilian has been training with the Under-21s and played and scored in their 2-2 EFL Trophy draw against Cheltenham last month.

Spurs will be desperate to sanction a move for Richarlison in January, and while a return to Brazil has been mooted, Palace could provide him with an opportunity to stay in the Premier League.

As Standard Sport reported, all options are on the table for Palace forward Jean-Philippe Mateta, and if the Frenchman was to leave, Palace would potentially be left looking for cover for Jorgen Strand Larsen.
