#1794. Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

“Brilliant technique,” said David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”

Only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

United should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” said Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their new sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

This is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

It could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

When Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

His substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

“I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes said. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

Everton 2 Manchester United 2 (Maitland-Niles) Stunning strike! Mazraoui had tackled Dewsbury-Hall in the box after more good work between Grealish and Hackney down the left. But the tackle diverted the ball to Maitland-Niles 25 yards out. And he wrapped his instep around a shot on debut that bent into the top left corner. What a goal!

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP

Grealish’s beguiling feet dazzle Mazraoui down the Everton left as he tricks him to reach the byline. He cuts back a pass to Barry who tees up Hackney for a shot that he wafts miles over the bar. Grealish gives him a look as if to say, “Really?”

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

Five minutes of added time for Everton to level again.

Everton 1 Manchester United 2 (Sesko) Sesko wins the ball in the middle and works it out to Bruno Fernandes running down the left. He stops, faces up Maitland-Niles and waits for Shaw to gallop past him before rolling it into the left-back’s stride. Shaw fizzes over a cross that parts Tarkowski’s luxuriant barnet and Sesko, lurking on his shoulder, buries it from eight yards.

Benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8

As Dominic says, below, Manchester United have been asking for this. They have been toothless since Mbeumo’s goal and the only significant threat, Rashford, was taken off for a left-back.

Everton 1 Man Utd 1 (George) A rasping, rising shot that beats Lammens at his near post. He absolutely larruped it after good work by Hackney to put him in space down the right of the box.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia

If you largely try and defend a 1-0 lead and don’t go for that second goal, there’s always the danger of that happening. Superb finish from George to equalise but it’s been so passive from United. Asking for trouble and they’ve got it. Big 7 minutes plus injury time for them now.

Free-kick on the left, parallel with the penalty spot. Hackney bends it in with his right and Branthwaite heads it on target but too close to Lammens who oddly elects to punch.

Mykolenko gives the ball back from the throw-in as Fernandes serves his minute on the sidelines.

Dalot is booked for pulling Grealish’s shirt when the left winger had spun him.

Maitland-Niles receives a warm reception. I had forgotten that he has five England caps.

Bruno Fernandes goes down after kicking Tarkowski’s studs when his foot was raised. The referee does not stop play but books Maguire for complaining when the ball eventually goes out.

Garner almost immediately goes down and starts stretching his calves.

Mykolenko hurls a long throw into the Man Utd box. Dewsbury-Hall meets it with a shot that he catches sweetly but hits a defender. The ball rebounds to Armstrong who scuffs his attempt wide .

George has switched to the right to accommodate Grealish. I wonder if there was ever a possibility of him returning to Villa? Would Unai Emery treasure him?

“He’s back!” the stadium announcer has proclaimed, as Jack Grealish has entered the fray. The move has provided an immediate bounce but let’s see what the former England man can do to change the pattern of the game. Everton believe they have got a £100m player. It’s time to show it.

Grealish’s first contribution sends Mykolenko away on an overlap and Martinez messes up his clearance from the cross, shanking it behind for a corner that they defend soundly.

Manchester United corner on the left after Tielemans’ 25-yard shot was deflected behind. Fernandes plays it along the ground to Shaw in the D. The left-back’s control spoons the ball up with his left so he improvises a right-foot volley with his swinger, dragging it predictably wide.

Rohl is beaten yet again by Rashford and works his way into the book after pulling him back. It’s been hard going for the Everton right back against Rashford but United just haven’t taken advantage of it enough.

Jack Grealish is stripped and ready to come on.

Rashford jinks at pace 35 yards up the inside-left channel, chopping to the left and barrelling between defenders. He takes it too wide to shoot so cutely backheels to Cunha who pulls back his left foot to shoot from six yards but Tarkowski slides his leg through his gait and pokes the ball away. The away fans shout for a penalty but Cunha has no complaints.

Barry diddles Martinez by feinting to the right and then darting left to open a rout to goal. He hammers a shot from about 16 yards that Shaw slides across to block, diverting it to Dewsbury-Hall whose follow-up effort is a tame daisycutter that Lammens easily gathers.

It threatened to be the case that a Manchester United goal would puncture the atmosphere completely and so it has proven. The likelihood here is the away team will score again in the next 10 minutes to completely kill the game. Everton have endured a miserable week and this flat performance is entirely in keeping with the narrative.

Johnson cuts in off the right to run on to Garner’s pass and shoots from 18 yards. Martinez makes himself as big as possible and the shot clips his calf, sending it up before it dips threateningly, whistling over the bar.

Mbeumo heads out Garner’s corner. Dewsbury-Hall crosses it back into the box and Tarkowski tries to head it across into the middle. Manchester United clear their lines.

Shaw slides in to block Dewsbury-Hall’s shot after the attacking midfielder had manipulated an opportunity with a quick interchange with Johnson.

Key for Manchester United, who have taken the lead in a match for the first time this season, not to let up on the tempo with which they started this half.

Everton respond with a menacing cross in from the left, from George, I think, that eludes Johnson as he arrives in the middle a second late.

Everton 0 Manchester United 1 (Mbeumo) United were probing patiently from the kick-off, Mainoo the hub until he helped the ball down the right and Mbeumo drove in from the right touchline, splitting George and Mykolenko until he reached the 18-yard line and wrapped his left instep around a shot that he arrowed into the bottom left corner.

A brilliant run and a fine finish from Bryan Mbeumo! 👏 pic.twitter.com/IM9kVcdPkh

We hadn’t seen that Mbeumo in the first half – so much better, driving inside at pace and with intent. Good decoy run from Fernandes. Top finish from Mbeumo.

Both managers will want to see a lot more urgency from their sides in the second half. Rashford has been United’s most threatening outlet and has the beating of Rohl but Mbeumo and Cunha were poor in those opening 45 minutes and both guilty of turning over the ball cheaply when United were breaking late in the first period. Barry should have hit the target with a header from Rohl’s cross. But it’s been a lacklustre game, low in quality so far.

A drab match that came to life in the last few minutes of the half, creating good a good chance for Thierno Barry and Jarrad Branthwaite thwarting Marcus Rashford and Bruno Fernandes. Everton look wide open on the right side of their defence and Brennan Johnson is starting to make headway against Luke Shaw.

Brilliant sliding tackle from Branthwaite when Rashford, piling down the inside-left channel in full flight. Just as he was about to pull the trigger, Branthwaite launched himself to knock it away and leapt back to his feet to block Fernandes’ stinging follow-up with the his head.

Mykolenko’s long throw from the left raises the Man Utd blood pressure as they try to scramble it clear. The ball pinballs around the six-yard box, comes off Dalot last and straight to Branthwaite who catches it straight and true but clips the shot at Lammens.

There will be three additional minutes. Barry and Johnson link up again to send the rangey striker down the right but again he hits his cross/shot straight at a defender at close quarters. He can’t work an angle but tries to go through a defender.

Rohl and Barry link up in more orthodox fashion with an excellent, dipping cross from the right-back. Barry peels off Maguire and thumps his header wide. That’s the best chance of the game.

Neat one-two between Johnson and Barry sends the latter into the box on the right but his shot/cross is fired straight at Shaw. The crowd shouts ‘Hand ball!’ but it wasn’t and the ref waves play on.

Everton have had no spark at all so far. George goes down when challenged by Mbeumo to give them a free-kick on the left, 35 yards from goal. Garner hits a floaty cross to the right of the box and Barry heads it wide.

It was Johnson who was under scrutiny for a ‘foul’ on Martinez’ but it was just a hand on the back.

Branthwaite is winded when he collides with Pickford in midair defending a back-post cross. Seems to be OK.

Fernandes whips over a cross and Armstrong beats Martínez to head it clear. VAR is looking at Martínez’s claim that he was fouled. Now it’s been cleared.

Yellow card for Johnson for sliding into Cunha’s stride and raising his right boot to leg him up right by the byline on the left, 12 inches outside the area.

Shaw trips Rohl in the Everton penalty area as they fought for the ball from Branthwaite’s block of Rashford’s superb cross from the left. The winger was looking for a near-post runner but Branthwaite read it perfectly, certainly better than Cunha, and telescoped out a leg to intercept.

Given the chaotic end to Everton’s transfer window, the atmosphere was going to go one of two ways: bearpit or flat as a pancake. As of now, it’s very much the latter situation, and not even a first sight of Jack Grealish has enabled the volume to be pumped up. Everton are finding it difficult and special attention will need to be paid to Harrison Armstrong, who has been harshly booked but must now walk a disciplinary tightrope. The young midfielder has played encouragingly once again and is desperate to impress.

Ripples of applause for Grealish who comes off the bench to warm up. Armstrong is urged to shoot when fed by Garner’s curling pass up the inside-right channel. But he dithers and then plays it out to Johnson whose cross is no good.

Best move of the game to date should have ended with Cunha hitting the target. The silkiest bit about it was how Rashford lulled Rohl into a false sense of security with his first touch then tapped the ball past him in the next movement just as Rohl was engaging. Very clever.

Now Shaw reaches the byline down the left and cuts it back for Fernandes. Branthwaite again to the rescue, diligently doing his job and closing down the Man Utd captain. Merlin Röhl is a talented player but he’s no right-back against the well-grooved Rashford and Shaw combo.

Dalot let the Rashford pass through his legs to Cunha, probably deliberately but he might have been better placed to apply the finish himself. Cunha had the time and space to do much better than he did, though.

Cunha blazes a side-foot shot from 18 yards over the bar. It was put on a plate by Rashford’s cut-back from the byline after the winger was sent down the flank by Mbeumo’s clever pass.

Manchester united again open up Everton through the middle when Mainoo slips a pass to Bruno Fernandes who puts his laces through a 25-yard shot that Branthwaite bravely throws himself at and deflects wide and out for a corner.

Tielemans’ eyes widen as space opens up between Armstrong and Garner but he scuffs his 22-yard shot which floats gently down Pickford’s throat.

Shaw cuts out Branthwaite’s long pass to Armstrong who was running down the inside-left channel. Manchester United do not clear their lines convincingly and Everton come back at them, probing away with George and Armstrong.

Dalot is let off a booking inexplicably for pulling George’s arm after being spun by Everton’s left-winger. The crowd is irate at that and seething even more when Armstrong is yellow-carded moments later for wrapping an arm around Fernandes’ neck to stop him running away.

Big shout for a home penalty when Barry goes down, face first in the six-yard box when closed down ny Martínez but it was more of a belly flop than a foul.

Slick attacking move from Manchester United, zipping a dozen passes around Everton and ending with Shaw being slid down the left by Rashford. The left-back crosses from the byline and Mbeumo cushions a header to Bruno Fernandes who flashes a sidewinder volley into the crossbar.

In the grand scheme of things, this might sound the most ridiculous complaint you have read but Manchester United’s kit - really? When they play away at Everton, their kit has always been – and always should be – red shirts, black shorts and black socks. It looks odd with two teams playing in white shorts. This may seem a random observation but there we go... there hasn’t been any action to discuss in the opening four minutes!

Maguire returns to the fray as Everton pass the ball through midfield to Johnson on the right. His cross, aiming for Barry, is cut out by Maguire and cleared to halfway. Back come Everton until Dewsbury-Hall is too rough with Mainoo as the Man Utd midfielder tackled him. Free-kick.

Lammens kicks the ball the full length of the field and Pickford picks it up. Mbeumo momentarily is at right-back with Dalot at centre-half.

Maguire is OK to continue but he will be off the field for the mandatory minute.

Maguire headed the back of Barry’s head and splattered his nose. He should be all right though he might need the cotton wool nostril bungs for a while, like Blackadder, the pencils and ‘wibble’.

Big cheers goes around the stadium when Harrison Armstrong’s name has read out. Everton would likely have sold him had there not been a backlash from fans opposing his sale.

Concern here for Harry Maguire. Looks in distress on the ground, laying very still. Concerned players around.

Leny Yoro is warming up on the touchline.

Looks like he caught the back of Barry’s head as he went to challenge. Sat up nose receiving treatment on a very bloodied nose.

Everton kick off, attacking from right to left. The fans, as usual, are making a racket. Everton work the ball back to Pickford who clips a diagonal up the left. Everton play it towards Barry who collides with Maguire who takes a blow to the head.

The teams emerge from the tunnel, both teams in their home kits with the only twist Manchester United’s switch to white socks.

We’re looking forward to seeing what [Brennan Johnson] does. We know he is very capable [and shown it] in recent seasons. Let’s hope he can bring us goals and assists as he did for Tottenham.

We’ve needed them [the two deadline day signings]. Maitland-Niles is physically fine. I don’t think Jack should be yet. We’ve needed it.

That’s all gone now [deadline day]. It’s all about the football. That’s what people are coming to see and we’ll have to play as well as we have done in our opening two games, get a positive result. Hopefully we can continue to build on it.

Nothing different [expected from the fans today]. They’re always really good for us.

No surprise United remain unchanged from the 5-2 win over Ipswich although Carrick will be looking for his side to score first here and make life a little easier for themselves after going behind to Hull and Ipswich in their opening two games. Brennan Johnson comes in for the departed Iliman Ndiaye, who joined Manchester City for £65m on deadline day. Jack Grealish is on the bench for Everton.

Moyes issued a call to arms to Everton fans in his programme notes after a dismal transfer window that has left him with just 18 outfield players. The Everton manager warning there may be difficult times to come.

“Finally, I must stress the importance of us all pulling together,” Moyes wrote.

“We need to be strong again and there may be occasions when we may have to find a way to get through some difficult moments.

“It is something you have all done in recent seasons. Everyone has pulled together for the good of the football club and we may need to do so again.”

We did a lot of good things [against Ipswich]. No two games are ever the same. We have different challenges today. We have to be ready for that with some slightly different ideas. But the boys did well last week, trained well this week and we’re really looking forward to it.

The next result is always the most important one regardless of what’s happened. Building momentum, building a run, of course it’s important. It’s game-by-game, as you know, but this is as tough as it comes for us, Everton away.

It’s not a major deal, we’ve got the squad and we can cope with it [increase in numbers of fixtures with the return to European football].

Everton  Pickford; Röhl, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry. Substitutes Travers, Maitland-Niles, Keane, Grealish, O’Brien, Dibling, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham.

Man Utd  Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martínez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Substitutes Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1793. Man Utd news: Red Devils 'plot ambitious move' to appoint new No.2 for Michael Carrick

By Carter White | 09 Nov 2026 16:54

Manchester United are reportedly interested in hiring Bayern Munich assistant Aaron Danks to help under-pressure head coach Michael Carrick.

The 20-time English champions are sitting in 18th position in the Premier League standings following a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at the Theatre of Dreams on Sunday afternoon, when the hosts completed another Old Trafford comeback.

Patrick Dorgu's last-minute equaliser was celebrated with considerable vigour, however, Man Utd remain in a worrying situation near the foot of the table, winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight contests.

It appears that the Red Devils have a real fight on their hands to retain their Premier League status, with United legend Roy Keane criticising head coach Carrick following the eight-goal thriller against Villa.

With the Premier League now taking a two-week break for international action, Man Utd have some time to recovery and prepare for a crunch clash with arch rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

According to TEAMtalk, Manchester United's hierarchy are set for 'high-level discussions' during the international break, analysing the start to the season and laying out a plan for the months ahead.

The future of head coach Carrick will be a major talking point for sporting director Jason Wilcox and head of recruitment Christopher Vivell, who have been sounding out potential replacements recently.

Former Newcastle United and Bournemouth boss Eddie Howe is supposedly of interest to Wilcox, whilst ex-Germany and Bayern Munich coach Julian Nagelsmann is said to have caught the eye of recruiter Vivell.

However, there is a reality in which Man Utd choose to stick with current leader Carrick, who has stated that he expects to take charge of the squad past the international break, despite an awful start to 2026-27.

It is understood that the club's boardroom are eyeing up a swoop for Bayern assistant Danks, who would arrive at the Theatre of Dreams to provide support for Carrick in his time of desperate need.

Working together at Championship outfit Middlesbrough in the past, Carrick and Danks possess a good footballing relationship, with the Bayern Munich man having plenty to offer the wounded English giants.

That being said, the direction of Red Devils travel is unlikely to change too much without significant change - whether that be to the playing staff or the people pulling the strings in the boardroom.

There is no doubt that the majority of United supporters would prefer a clean break from Carrick's faltering plans, instead of an attempt to strengthen the 45-year-old's backroom ranks.

#1792. Man United transfer news: Red Devils could move for "quick" and "powerful" Premier League centre-back next summer

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 17:59, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 18:03

Manchester United are reportedly huge admirers of Nottingham Forest's Murillo and could make a move for the centre-back during next summer's transfer window.

Murillo, 24, has provided one assist in 11 appearances for Forest this season, while he has represented the Reds on 125 occasions since arriving from Corinthians in the summer of 2023.

According to Man United's former chief scout Mick Brown, Man United have been keen on the Brazilian "for quite a long time now", and a "huge offer" could potentially be forthcoming at the end of the 2026-27 campaign.

"Murillo is somebody Man United have liked for quite a long time now," Brown told Football Insider. "Obviously they're not the only ones, because at his best he is a top class player, and he would certainly be an improvement on the players they've got at the moment.

"He's quick, powerful, aggressive, excellent on the ball, can pass, isn't afraid to get stuck in, it's pretty much everything you want from a centre-back. At his best, when you compare him to Lisandro Martinez who plays in the same position, there's such a big difference in quality.

"So for Man United, he is somebody they're going to be very keen on and I have a feeling that if they came in with a huge offer, it would give Forest something to consider.

"They're a good side, Forest, but they're down the wrong end of the table and if that continues then their best players might be tempted away.

"If there are any suggestions that Murillo could be allowed to move, then Man United should be all over it, because he would be such a big improvement for them."

Murillo has made 103 Premier League appearances for Forest, scoring three goals and registering three assists in the process.

Man United are set to overhaul their defence at the end of the season, and it is not impossible to imagine three new centre-backs arriving at the club.

Both Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire are out of contract next summer and could leave on free transfers, while a decision needs to be made on Matthijs de Ligt, who has recently returned to action after almost a year on the sidelines through injury.

Man United are also set to bring in a new left-back and right-back next summer as part of a major revamp, with Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot both potentially moving on.

#1791. Genoa 1-2 AC Milan: Cisse and Pulisic score in hard-fought victory

AC Milan secured a much-needed three points on Sunday afternoon as they beat an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.

The groundwork for the victory was laid in the first half, when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot to get his eighth of the campaign, before Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos after a stray pass inside the box.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike, but Milan did ultimately manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

It means that a top four spot has been reclaimed for the time being while waiting to see how the game between Inter and Como plays out, and it eases some of the pressure heading into the international break.

Ruben Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa started on the front foot and they immediately created an opening inside the first minute. Koni De Winter allowed Osmajic to run off his shoulder and get a shot off from the left side of the box, but Maignan watched it roll narrowly wide of the far post.

One minute after Vitinha had back-heeled a near-post cross into Maignan’s hands, Milan created their first opening. Pulisic’s cross from the byline wasn’t well-aimed but the clearance fell straight to Ramos, who didn’t quite connect right with his effort and sent it a couple of yards wide of the far post.

Milan continued to knock on the door and Ramos almost found himself on the end of a golden opportunity when Gila was found on the overlap and provided a cut-back, though Marcandalli did brilliantly to cut out the danger.

Then, in the 13th minute, Milan did take the lead through Alphadjo Cisse. The goal was assisted by Adrien Rabiot who found the run of the Italian with a nice square ball, but Pulisic was the one who won possession back on the high press to create the opportunity, which was well finished by Cisse for his eighth goal of the campaign.

In the 19th minute, the Rossoneri doubled their lead. Another successful press forced Ostigard into a mistake as his square ball back towards the goalkeeper was cut off by Ramos. The Portuguese squared to Pulisic after evading a defender, and the American made no mistake as he fired inside the near post to make it 2-0.

Right on the half-hour mark, Genoa thought they had got themselves back into the game when Osmajic headed past Maignan having escaped his man to be found by Vitinha’s flick-on. However, the offside flag was raised and the decision was upheld, though it looked very close.

Despite being two goals up, Milan never gave the impression of being in control and Genoa had a couple of half-chances towards the end of the half, including an Ostigard header that Maignan managed to claim.

The start to the second half was certainly a fractious one, and the Milan players were surrounding the referee Davide Massa five minutes into it when Rabiot seized on a loose touch from Marcandalli to run in behind.

He was dragged back by the defender who appeared to be the last man, but a yellow card was deemed to be sufficient. Rabiot got a yellow too for his protests, and three members of the Milan coaching staff were shown a red.

Amorim opted to make a couple of changes on the hour mark, with Cisse making way for Omari Hutchinson and Diawara coming off for Filippo Terracciano.

As the game entered the final 20 minutes, Milan began to look comfortable with their lead but at times complacent too. Musah gave possession away in the left-back position and it gave Vitinha a dangerous position to get a shot off, though Maignan did well to parry it away.

The pressure continued to come from the Rossoblu, and El Shaarawy had a chance off the bench when a cross found him in the box. He brought it down well, but Terracciano got a knee to it to deflect it over. Pulisic made way for Ardon Jashari after.

Inside the final few minutes Pervis Estupinan became the last player to come, replacing Musah. The sub was made just before El Shaarawy lined up a free-kick from about 22 yards out, and it would yield Genoa’s route back into the game.

The initial shot was blocked as it went into a crowd but was not cleared, allowing Ellertsson all the time in the world to step up and strike one from distance that nestled inside the right post with Maignan rooted. Game on with two minutes of normal time left.

Malo Gusto is open to a move away from Chelsea in January, according to a report from The BBC.

While the French international might have made 34 Premier League appearances last season, Gusto has drastically struggled to hold down a regular spot under Xabi Alonso.

Although Chelsea skipper Reece James might be recovering from yet another long-term injury issue, the 23-year-old has not made a Premier League start in almost two months and The BBC are suggesting that Gusto is growing increasingly frustrated in west London.

#1789. Michael Carrick future: Review 'ongoing' at Man United - what will be the outcome?

By Matt Law | 09 Nov 2026 18:27, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 18:29

Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox is reportedly leading the review into Michael Carrick's future at Old Trafford.

A disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, with the team winning just one of their first 10 league games of the season.

Man United did manage to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League last week, though, before twice coming from two goals behind to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, and the season has now been interrupted by an international break.

There is huge uncertainty when it comes to Carrick's future, with the sporting department at Old Trafford now reviewing the head coach's position.

According to The Guardian, Wilcox is leading the review, with chief executive Omar Berrada also being consulted, before a recommendation is made to Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Carrick was expected to be sacked by Man United off the back of the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on October 25, but he was allegedly given three games to save his job - the trip to Chelsea in the Premier League, followed by the games against Roma and Villa.

It is understood that Eddie Howe is Wilcox's number one choice to replace Carrick, should a change be made, but that is not thought to be a view universally shared by the decision-makers.

Man United are next in action at Anfield on November 22, facing Liverpool in the Premier League, before tackling Sporting Lisbon away from home in the Champions League.

November will then conclude with a home league game against Brentford.

"We’re in November. I don’t like the situation we’re in or the results we’ve had, but we can definitely do something about it. We haven’t won enough games but I expect to move forward," Carrick told Sky Sports News after the draw with Villa.

"We’ll keep working on the things we’ve been working on, and tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches."

The positions of both Wilcox and Berrada have also been called into question due to Man United's ongoing struggles, and the pair are facing uncertain futures.

There remain calls from the club's supporters for the Glazer family to sell their share of the 20-time English champions, but there are no indications at this stage that will occur.

As it stands, Carrick is likely to remain in charge of Man United for the Liverpool game, with the Englishman still being backed despite the team's struggles this season.

#1788. Player Ratings: Genoa 1-2 AC Milan – De Winter, Pulisic and Rabiot take charge

AC Milan responded to the criticism with an important win at Genoa on Sunday afternoon. A few players made the difference and below are the ratings for the Rossoneri.

After the mid-week failure against Ferencvaros, Milan knew that three points were more or less a must against Genoa. Thankfully, aside from a dramatic ending, it was a comfortable game for the Rossoneri and a few of the players also got to send some strong signals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

If you haven’t already, make sure to check out how we decide the player ratings. From the scale to what affects the rating, we have compiled everything there.

🥇 Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

👎 Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

👔 Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

Maignan (6.5): We saw a couple of good stops from him, including one on Vitinha in the second half, and his distribution was decent. He couldn’t really do anything about the goal either, as it was a really good effort from Ellertsson.

Gila (6): I liked his performance overall but there were a couple of moments that dragged down the rating for me, more specifically the fouls he committed. Put simply, he was a bit too rash and it was after one of the free-kicks he caused that Genoa scored their goal.

De Winter (7.5): The only poor moment came inside the first 60 seconds, when he was caught out a bit by a ball over the top, but he managed to track back and at least narrow the angle. After that, he was brilliant in his positioning, showing off with some great tackles and interceptions too. Really good.

Diawara (6): He was carded for a very rash challenge, but apart from that, he kept his calm at the back and had decent positioning throughout. It’s not like Genoa threatened Milan a lot, but enough for a pass here still.

Moreira (6.5): It was a lively start from him, I would say, with some good moments on that right flank. However, the end product wasn’t always amazing (some blocked shots), and he faded a bit attacking-wise as the game went on. Solid though and he did put in a defensive shift at the end.

Modric (7): We got to see some really nice flicks and quick play from him today. Defensively, he contributed as well, which was especially clear with a last-ditch toe-poke to avoid a 1v1 for Genoa. There was one poor pass into the middle which could have proved costly, but the rest was good.

Rabiot (7.5): He was back to his usual self today after what was a subpar display against Ferencvaros. Great movement between the lines and elegance on the ball were his main strengths, also getting the assist for the opener.

Musah (6): We have to praise him for doing well in a ‘new’ position, following the instructions from Amorim nearly perfectly. What stopped him from getting a higher rating here was the big giveaway at the end, which Genoa really should have done more with.

Pulisic (7.5 – MOTM): He did really well to keep his composure after receiving the ball from Ramos, making things comfortable with a two-goal lead. He was also the man who won back the ball before the first goal. In addition to the goals, it felt like he was always available and definitely helped Milan keep possession.

Cisse (7): It was a very tidy finish to give Milan the lead, showing once again that he knows how to turn up in the right place at the right time. However, for a higher rating, I would have liked to see more in his 1v1s, which weren’t always so successful.

Ramos (5.5): I’m torn here. It was unselfish to pass to Pulisic for the second goal rather than shooting himself, so that deserves praise. However, I actually think he was very sloppy in open play with heavy touches and positioning that sometimes left a lot to be desired. I suppose the big question is how much his defensive work rate is worth to the rating.

Terracciano (6): Surprisingly good! He had a crucial deflection on a shot from El Shaarawy and also headed the ball away quite a few times in the end, certainly contributing to the three points.

Hutchinson (5.5): He was the worst for me, as he didn’t really add anything in attack and also failed to run down the clock at the end. It’s a shame because there was space to exploit when Genoa pushed forward.

Jashari (6): We didn’t see much in terms of attacking contributions and build-up, since he came on with ten minutes to go, but he was responsible for a few clearances at the end.

Estupinan (5.5): I don’t think it was much of a foul, but in those moments, you shouldn’t even give the referee the opportunity to blow the whistle. He knows that.

Amorim (6): Fielding Musah on the left actually worked out well, so kudos for that one. The rest of the eleven pretty much picked itself and tactically, while it was a good game, it wasn’t anything extraordinary. But his pre-match message seemed to work, as the players showed more desire.

By Darren Plant | 09 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 09 Nov 2026 19:05

Leicester City have been handed an away tie at National League South team Dover Athletic in the FA Cup second round.

On Friday night, the Foxes came through a testing encounter at National League North outfit Oxford City with a 4-2 victory, and Russell Martin's side will again be on their travels to face a non-league club in the next round of the competition.

Meanwhile, Luton Town will make the trip to the North-West to face National League team AFC Fylde.

Wimborne Town, the Southern Premier South side who stunned Crawley Town over the weekend, have been handed the reward of a home showdown with League One giants Bradford City.

Northern Premier League club Guiseley will host Notts County, while Kidderminster Harriers will make the long trip to Barrow.

The winner of the all seventh-tier tie between Plymouth Parkway and Berkhamsted - which will be played on Monday night - will face League Two side Barnet.

These ties will take place between December 4 and December 7.

#1786. 'People keep telling me it's great I'm managing against my son... it's not - it's horrible': Peterborough boss ROBBIE SAVAGE and Reading star CHARLIE on their 'awkward' FA Cup showdown, playing for Man United and dangers facing modern young players

Published: 02:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 09:02 EST, 7 November 2026

The FA Cup cast its spell upon the Savages while they were out shopping for groceries.

Reading midfielder Charlie was strolling the aisles of the Marks & Spencer foodhall with his girlfriend when his phone began to buzz. He remembered it was first-round draw day.

He fished out the phone, saw the cascade of messages and realised, as they like to say in M&S, this was not just any FA Cup draw. He called his dad.

Peterborough United boss Robbie was in the Co-op. He had stopped on his way back to the rented lodgings he describes as a 'little annexe in someone's garden' and was rummaging through the ready meals in search of a spaghetti bolognese for one when he answered.

'The reception in Peterborough isn't great, it kept cutting out,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'Charlie said: "You won't believe the draw." I thought he was going to say Forest Green. Or Macclesfield. I didn't think about Reading. He said: "You've got us." I just went: "Oh no."'

They were on a collision course from the moment Robbie left Forest Green for the Posh job last month. The teams were scheduled to meet in League One next month at Reading but the FA Cup draw caught them off guard.

Peterborough boss Robbie Savage (right) with his son, Reading midfielder Charlie. The pair will meet in the FA Cup first round at London Road on Saturday

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling,' Robbie tells Daily Mail Sport

And while they were both at great pains to stress that Saturday's tie at London Road, screened live on TNT Sports, is about Peterborough and Reading not their little family gathering, they can appreciate the fuss.

'Football is a beautiful game, it brings people together and creates rivalries,' says Charlie. 'This week it's created a rivalry in our family. I'm not sure who my mum, brother, grandparents and cousins will support but there's no better time for them to have a half-and-half scarf.'

For Robbie, the beauty of the occasion is yet to unfurl itself. 'It's going to be horrible,' he says. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

'This will be the first time I hope my son doesn't have an impact, which is a horrible feeling. People keep telling me it's great. I've got to say it's not great, it's horrible. Usually we speak every day and I've not been able to speak to him all week because I don't want to put him in a position where anything gets out and anyone can point a finger at him.

'I don't want it to be billed as Savage v Savage because it's not. Charlie might not play but if he plays and makes a mistake and we score the winner, so be it. If he plays and scores the winner, well, wow.'

Robbie puffs out his cheeks and widens his eyes as he considers this scenario. 'We've got to win for Peterborough United,' he adds.

Ironically, it was a passion relit by coaching his sons which tempted the former Leicester, Birmingham and Blackburn midfielder out of the comfort of his media work and into coaching. Savage helped out with his youngest son Freddie's Under 13s team in the Timperley and District Junior Sunday League.

'Standing out at training on a Tuesday and Thursday night,' says Robbie. 'Sunday morning, putting the nets up. I've been that dad. In the first season we were hammered 13-0, but we built a team and won a lot of things.'

Charlie Savage in action for Reading. The midfielder played 45 games for the club last season but has yet to start a league match during this campaign

Savage offers some advice to his team in his new role as manager of Peterborough

Two years ago, Charlie and Freddie implored their father to follow his heart and make the switch from sporting director to manager at Macclesfield in the Northern Premier League.

'Even back then, he said one day he'd manage against me,' Charlie tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I was in League One and he was in Step Three and I'm thinking, "Well, give it a few years", but he always gets where he wants to get to.

'He's a competitor. He wants to win, wants to succeed. Even with my little brother's team it hurt him to lose in Sunday morning grassroots football. That's something inside him and it won't change.

'He will want to beat us. Unfortunately for him, I'm the same. I want to win. There might be an awkward car journey home.'

Charlie's memories of his father playing football are from Derby, the last stop of a 15-year professional career which started at Manchester United and took in seven different clubs, as well as 39 Wales caps. 'I remember seeing his long hair, scurrying around the pitch,' says the 23-year-old. 'Throwing his arms up and shouting at the refs.'

Like his dad, Charlie also came through United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

'He'll always have that on me,' says Robbie. 'All I ever wanted to do from 14 to 19 was play for one minute in Manchester United's first team. It didn't happen and he's done it. His name is on the wall at Carrington and mine isn't.

'I'm so glad his name is there instead of mine. You want the best for your sons. I'm proud of both my sons.'

Charlie has three Wales caps and counting. His father won 39...

...but despite both Charlie and Robbie coming through the Manchester United academy, only Charlie played for the first team (above), against Young Boys at Old Trafford in 2021

Freddie is studying for an economics degree at the University of Manchester. Charlie left United for Reading four years ago and now has 175 senior appearances and three Wales caps under his belt and a reputation in his own right.

'He's got a great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie. 'He's intelligent. Nine As in his GCSEs. He doesn't drink, he lives his life 24 hours a day, seven days a week to be a footballer. He's a down-to-earth, humble kid.

'He was so brave to go and play senior football when he had three years left at Manchester United, and it's paid off. He played 45 games last season. He hasn't started a league game this season but hasn't sulked.

'I was a sulker, as Martin O'Neill and Nigel Clough (who coached Savage at Leicester and Derby respectively) will tell you. If that was me, my body language would be negative, but he's got a great attitude. And I've tried to tell him now he has to train harder than ever and conduct himself in the right way.'

If Robbie is a guiding light and inspiration for Charlie, vital information flows both ways for an aspiring manager with a young team.

'The mindset of a Millennial is completely different to when I played,' says the 52-year-old Posh boss. 'If they're not in the team or the manager has shouted at them, they go home to an apartment where they live alone away from their families, isolated from 2pm to 7am with all that time to think about it.

'We have to understand their vulnerabilities on and off the pitch. Charlie has been through that so without knowing it, he's made me a better manager. I try to think about what's best for my players, what I'd want a manager to do for Charlie in that situation.'

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end,' Charlie says of his dad Robbie

'Great left foot, passing range and incredible running ability,' says Robbie of his son Charlie

Being the Son of Sav cannot be easy. Not only the added scrutiny and expectation, and accusations doors have been opened for him by a famous and influential father, but also in a world where footballers are too often considered fair game for abuse whether inside the stadium or online.

'It's there in all forms of life,' admits Charlie. 'Maybe people subconsciously want me to fail a little bit more because of who he is. I get it. Football is a game and my dad is a divisive figure inside that game.

'He gives it out and he can take it and, unfortunately, it has become part of his life to be on the receiving end. Sometimes the abuse goes too far. People forget he's a human not just a football personality.

'But I wouldn't change who he is. I wouldn't change having him as my dad, I'm very proud of him.'

#1785. Bellingham brothers’ England link-up would be ’emotional’ for Jobe

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jobe Bellingham says an England link-up with his brother Jude would be "emotional".

The younger Bellingham brother was a surprise call-up for Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

Jobe played a key role in Sunderland's promotion to the Premier League in 2025, but then followed in Jude's footsteps by joining Borussia Dortmund.

He played 45 games for BVB last term, making 29 starts and providing three assists. This season, Jobe has made 15 appearances for Dortmund, recording three assists, though the 21-year-old is yet to score for the Bundesliga giants.

However, Jobe is now on the verge of his first senior England cap, meaning the Bellingham siblings would join the list of brothers to play for the Three Lions.

Which of our #ThreeLions' morning routines do you agree with? https://t.co/QNiM9GhEJS

The last occasion came when Trevoh Chalobah followed on from his brother Nathaniel (2018) in earning an England cap last year. The last brothers to play at the same time for England, though, were Gary and Phil Neville.

"I can't ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it's a great, great feeling for the family," Jobe said on the Football Association's England app.

"It's quite special, to be honest. It's such a huge bonus on top of something that's already so special and so great.

"To be called up for England is a dream itself and I've been so proud to have the opportunity to represent England at every age group. I always enjoyed coming away with England, I love competing against top players at whichever age group.

"But to have that chance of an opportunity to represent England with my brother, it's really hard to put into words.

"I don't have the words, really. I think it's only emotion that could describe it, and, hopefully, if that time does come, you'll see a lot of emotion from people, and definitely from my family."

The Bellinghams would become the 22nd sets of brothers to feature for England.
